Data for 54 students showed no differences in scores between groups on any parameter. No specific concerns related to the absence of general surgery were identified.

The medical files of all medicine and surgery residents in their first year of specialization between the years 2005 and 2008 were reviewed. These residents were required to go through a preventive medical visit at the University Center of Family and Community Health.
results.reference: Effective undergraduate surgical education can be offered in many specialty settings. Removal of the requirement for general surgery in clerkship may lead to a more effective use of all educational opportunities. A careful analysis of local programs and facilities is necessary before suggesting this change to other institutions.

results.question: Is Acupuncture Efficacious for Treating Phonotraumatic Vocal Pathologies?
rewritten_queries: acupuncture phonotraumatic vocal pathologies treatment efficacy
acupuncture vocal fold nodules polyps clinical trials
acupuncture voice disorder therapy outcomes
results.answer:
The study described shows that both genuine and sham acupuncture groups experienced significant improvement in vocal function and quality of life, but only the genuine acupuncture group demonstrated structural improvements with a significant reduction in the size of vocal fold lesions. This indicates that acupuncture is effective in treating phonotraumatic vocal pathologies, particularly in reducing lesion size.

yes
contexts: To investigate the effectiveness of acupuncture in treating phonotraumatic vocal fold lesions.STUDY DESIGN/

A total of 123 dysphonic individuals with benign vocal pathologies were recruited. They were given either genuine acupuncture (n = 40), sham acupuncture (n = 44), or no treatment (n = 39) for 6 weeks (two 30-minute sessions/wk). The genuine acupuncture group received needles puncturing nine voice-related acupoints for 30 minutes, two times a week for 6 weeks, whereas the sham acupuncture group received blunted needles stimulating the skin surface of the nine acupoints for the same frequency and duration. The no-treatment group did not receive any intervention but attended just the assessment sessions. One-hundred seventeen subjects completed the study (genuine acupuncture = 40; sham acupuncture = 43; and no treatment = 34), but only 84 of them had a complete set of vocal functions and quality of life measures (genuine acupuncture = 29; sham acupuncture = 33; and no-treatment = 22) and 42 of them with a complete set of endoscopic data (genuine acupuncture = 16; sham acupuncture = 15; and no treatment = 11).

Significant improvement in vocal function, as indicated by the maximum fundamental frequency produced, and also perceived quality of life, were found in both the genuine and sham acupuncture groups, but not in the no-treatment group. Structural (morphological) improvements were, however, only noticed in the genuine acupuncture group, which demonstrated a significant reduction in the size of the vocal fold lesions.

All patients (606 joints) had successful TMJ (temporomandibular joint) surgeries through the VMPA (vascular-guided multilayer preauricular approach). All incisions healed favorably with an uneventful recovery. No patient developed permanent weakness of the facial nerve or other severe complications.
To test the hypothesis that increasing the nerve length within the treatment volume for trigeminal neuralgia radiosurgery would improve pain relief.
results.reference: The findings showed that acupuncture of voice-related acupoints could bring about improvement in vocal function and healing of vocal fold lesions.

results.question: Is aneurysm repair justified for the patients aged 80 or older after aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage?
rewritten_queries: aneurysm repair outcomes elderly patients 80 years and older
aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage treatment elderly
surgical vs conservative management aneurysmal SAH octogenarians
results.answer:
The study reviewed 69 cases aged 80 or older with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage and found that those who received aneurysm repair (clipping or coil embolization) had significantly better clinical outcomes compared to those treated conservatively. There was no difference in initial severity or premorbid status between groups, supporting the benefit of surgical intervention in this age group.

yes
contexts: We reviewed 500 consecutive cases with acute aSAH (aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage) with surgical indication for aneurysm repair. Inoperable cases such as dead-on-arrival and the cases with both pupils dilated were excluded. We compared the cases aged 80 or older that received clipping or coil embolization with the controls that the family selected conservative treatment.

With the advancement of an aging society in the world, an increasing number of elderly patients have been hospitalized due to aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH (aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage)). There is no study that compares the elderly cases of aSAH (aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage) who receive the definitive treatment with those who treated conservatively. The aim of this study was to investigate the feasibility of the definitive surgery for the acute subarachnoid cases aged 80 or older.

A 52-year-old woman underwent a craniotomy for a ruptured internal carotid aneurysm. A computed tomography scan showed that SAH (subarachnoid hemorrhage) existed predominantly in the posterior fossa and subdural hematoma beneath the cerebellar tentorium. Intrathecal administration of urokinase, IV administration of fasudil hydrochloride, and continuous cerebrospinal fluid (CSF (cerebrospinal fluid)) evacuation via cisternal drainage were performed as prophylactic treatments for vasospasm. On the sixth postoperative day, the patient complained of severe lower back and buttock pain. Magnetic resonance imaging showed a subdural hematoma in the lumbosacral region. Although the mass effect was extensive, the patient showed no neurologic symptoms other than the sciatica. She was treated conservatively. The hematoma dissolved gradually and had diminished completely 15 weeks later. Her pain gradually subsided, and she was discharged 7 weeks later without any neurologic deficit.

A case of spinal subdural hematoma (SSDH (spinal subdural hematoma)) following subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH (subarachnoid hemorrhage)) because of a ruptured internal carotid aneurysm is described. Such a case has never been reported.

69 cases were included in this study (ranged 80-98, male:female=9:60). 56 cases (81.2%) had an aneurysm in the anterior circulation. 23 cases received clipping, 20 cases coil embolization and 26 cases treated conservatively. The cases with aneurysm repair showed significantly better clinical outcome than the controls, while World Federation of Neurological Surgeons (WFNS (world federation of neurological surgeons)) grade on admission and premorbid modified Rankin Scale showed no difference between them.
results.reference: Better prognosis was obtained when ruptured aneurysm was repaired in the elderly than it was treated conservatively. From the results of this study, we should not hesitate to offer the definitive surgery for the elderly with aSAH.

results.question: Do general practice characteristics influence uptake of an information technology (IT) innovation in primary care?
rewritten_queries: general practice characteristics IT innovation adoption primary care
factors influencing health IT uptake general practice
primary care technology implementation barriers facilitators
results.answer:
The evidence indicates that most general practice structural characteristics (such as list size, training status, number of GPs, GP age, gender, deprivation level) were not associated with the uptake of the web-based clinical information system. However, the number of diabetes-educated staff was consistently linked to increased use by both nurses and GPs, suggesting that specific staff training influences IT innovation uptake rather than broader practice characteristics.

yes
contexts: Recent evaluations of IT innovations in primary care have highlighted variations between centres and practices in uptake and use. We evaluated whether structural characteristics of a general practice were associated with variations in use of a web-based clinical information system underpinning a Managed Clinical Network in diabetes, between the years 2001 and 2003.

Initially there were a few practices which made very frequent use of the information system, with relatively high numbers of practices using the facility infrequently. However, overall use gradually became more evenly spread. This effect was particularly evident among nurse users. Frequent use by GPs was evident in only a small number of practices, with mean GP (general practitioner) use decreasing over the three years. In linear regression analyses, none of the general practice variables were associated with online use, either overall or stratified by staff type, except for the numbers of diabetes-educated staff. This was consistently associated with increased use by nurses and GPs.

As part of an MRC funded study into primary care oral anticoagulation management, INR (international normalized ratio) measurements obtained in general practice were validated against values on the same samples obtained in hospital laboratories. A prospective comparative trial was undertaken between three hospital laboratories and nine general practices. All patients attending general practice based anticoagulant clinics had parallel INR (international normalized ratio) estimations performed in general practice and in a hospital laboratory.

Using a computerised audit trail, we calculated the numbers of web-based operations that occurred in each practice, stratified by staff type and year, and adjusted for the numbers of registered diabetic patients. In regression analyses, we determined whether total use was associated with structural characteristics of the practice (total list size, training status, numbers of GPs (general practitioners), mean age of the GPs, numbers of female GPs, level of deprivation of the population and whether staff had received advanced training in diabetes care).

In a population-based cohort study using register data, we analysed the prescribing of new drugs by Danish general practitioners. Angiotensin-II antagonists, triptans, selective cyclo-oxygenase-2 antagonists and esomeprazol were used in the assessment. As indicators of new drug uptake, we used adoption time, cumulative incidence, preference proportion, incidence rate and prescription cost and volume. For each measure, we ranked the general practices. Ranks were pair-wise plotted, and Pearson's correlation coefficient ( r) was calculated. Next, we analysed the correlation between ranks across different drug classes.
results.reference: The analyses show that structural characteristics of a practice are not associated with uptake of a new IT facility, but that its use may be influenced by post-graduate education in the relevant clinical condition. For this diabetes system at least, practice nurse use was critical in spreading uptake beyond initial GP enthusiasts and for sustained and rising use in subsequent years.

results.question: Prognosis of well differentiated small hepatocellular carcinoma--is well differentiated hepatocellular carcinoma clinically early cancer?
rewritten_queries: well differentiated small hepatocellular carcinoma prognosis
well differentiated hepatocellular carcinoma clinical stage early cancer
results.answer:
The histological analysis in the provided abstracts indicates that well differentiated (w-d) hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) shows lower incidences of fibrous capsule formation and intact portal veins, but there were no significant differences in intrahepatic metastasis, portal vein invasion, or disease-free survival compared to less differentiated HCC. Additionally, the presence of minute cancerous foci at the time of operation suggests that w-d HCC may not be clinically early cancer despite its differentiation status.

no
contexts: The purpose of this study is to examine whether or not well differentiated (w-d) hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC (hepatocellular carcinoma)) is indeed clinically early cancer.

We identified 94,173 patients with small cell carcinoma of which 88,605 (94.1%) and 5,568 (5.9%) had pulmonary small cell carcinoma and EPSCC (extrapulmonary small cell carcinomas), respectively. EPSCC (extrapulmonary small cell carcinomas) patients were subdivided by site with the following proportions: genitourinary (24.1%), gastrointestinal (22.1%), head and neck (7.1%), breast (4%), and miscellaneous (42.7%). Overall EPSSC and specifically gastrointestinal disease had significantly improved median, 5- and 10-year survival with surgery and/or radiation for all stages and sizes. For all EPSCCs multivariate analysis revealed age (>50), gender (female), stage (regional, distant), radiation, and surgery to be independent predictors of survival.
The purpose of this paper is to evaluate the efficacy of ultrasonographic screening for primary hepatocellular carcinoma.

The histological analysis revealed that w-d HCCs had lower incidences of fibrous capsule formation (P<0.01), when compared to l-d HCCs. There were no significant differences in the incidence of intrahepatic metastasis, or portal vein invasion. In a resected specimen of w-d HCC (hepatocellular carcinoma), barium sulfate and gelatin were injected into portal vein and a transparent specimen was made. The transparent specimen showed that the portal vein in the tumor seemed to be intact. Microscopically, cancer cell infiltration into the fibrous frame of the portal tract was present. There were no significant differences in the disease free survival between the two groups. An analysis of tumor volume doubling time in recurrent foci suggested that minute cancerous foci had been present at the time of operation.

Patients enrolled in the study had been diagnosed with non-small cell carcinoma in stages IV or IIIB with pleural or N2-N3 involvement and with a performance status of 2 or below according to the Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG (eastern cooperative oncology group)). Survival was analyzed with regard to the following variables: age, sex, comorbidity, weight loss, laboratory test results, histological type, ECOG (eastern cooperative oncology group) score, TNM staging, and treatment. The Student t test, the chi(2) test, the Kaplan-Meier method, the log-rank test, and Cox regression analysis were used in the statistical analysis.
results.reference: W-d HCCs were clinically demonstrated not to be early cancer, because there was no significant difference in disease free survival between the patients with w-d and l-d HCCs.

results.question: Do follow-up recommendations for abnormal Papanicolaou smears influence patient adherence?
rewritten_queries: follow-up recommendations abnormal Pap smear patient adherence
cervical cancer screening follow-up compliance factors
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that adherence to follow-up recommendations after abnormal Pap smears is influenced by factors such as the number of patient reminders and insurance status. Specifically, the use of up to three patient reminders substantially improved adherence, suggesting that follow-up recommendations and the manner in which they are communicated do influence patient adherence. Therefore, the evidence supports that follow-up recommendations do influence adherence.

yes
contexts: To compare adherence to follow-up recommendations for colposcopy or repeated Papanicolaou (Pap) smears for women with previously abnormal Pap smear results.

The rate of overall adherence to follow-up recommendations was 56.0% (136/243). Adherence to a second colposcopy was not significantly different from that to a repeated Pap smear (odds ratio, 1.40; 95% confidence interval, 0.80-2.46). The use of as many as 3 patient reminders substantially improved adherence to follow-up. Women without insurance and women attending 1 of the 3 clinics were less likely to adhere to any follow-up recommendation (hazard ratio for no insurance, 0.43 [95% confidence interval, 0.20-0.93], and for clinic, 0.35 [95% confidence interval, 0.15-0.73]).

Documented adherence to follow-up within 8 months of an abnormal result. Attempts to contact the patients for follow-up, adherence to follow-up recommendations, and patient characteristics were abstracted from medical records. The probability of adherence to follow-up vs the number of follow-up attempts was modeled with survival analysis. Cox proportional hazards models were used to examine multivariate relationships related to adherence.

Updated guidelines for the screening and management of cervical cancer in the United States recommend starting Papanicolaou (Pap) testing at age 21 and screening less frequently with less aggressive management for abnormalities. We sought to examine updated Pap test screening guidelines and how they may affect the detection of invasive cervical cancer, especially among women<30 years of age.
Routine clinic protocols for follow-up--telephone call, letter, or certified letter--were applied without regard to the type of abnormality seen on a Pap smear or recommended examination.
results.reference: Adherence to follow-up was low in this family planning clinic population, no matter what type of follow-up was advised. Adherence was improved by the use of up to 3 reminders. Allocating resources to effective methods for improving adherence to follow-up of abnormal results may be more important than which follow-up procedure is recommended.

results.question: Biomolecular identification of allergenic pollen: a new perspective for aerobiological monitoring?
rewritten_queries: biomolecular methods allergenic pollen identification
aerobiological monitoring pollen detection techniques
molecular markers pollen allergens aerobiology
results.answer:
The provided abstracts describe the development and testing of a real-time PCR method for detecting and quantifying airborne allergenic pollen, which offers a rapid, accurate, and automated alternative to traditional morphological identification. This biomolecular approach successfully identified pollen taxa and performed preliminary quantification, suggesting it is a promising new perspective for aerobiological monitoring.

yes
contexts: To verify the feasibility of developing a real-time polymerase chain reaction (PCR (polymerase chain reaction)) approach, an alternative to optical analysis, as a rapid, accurate, and automated tool for the detection and quantification of airborne allergenic pollen taxa.

Accurate and updated information on airborne pollen in specific areas can help allergic patients. Current monitoring systems are based on a morphologic identification approach, a time-consuming method that may represent a limiting factor for sampling network enhancement.

The setup of a modified DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid) extraction protocol allowed us to achieve good-quality pollen DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid). Taxon-specific nuclear gene fragments were identified and sequenced. Designed primer pairs and probes identified selected pollen taxa, mostly at the required classification level. Pollen was properly identified even when collected on routine aerobiological tape. Preliminary quantification assays on pollen grains were successfully performed on test species and in mixes.

The traditional cetyl trimethyl ammonium bromide-based method was modified for DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid) isolation from pollen. Taxon-specific DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid) sequences were identified via bioinformatics or literature searches and were PCR (polymerase chain reaction) amplified from the matching allergenic taxa; based on the sequences of PCR (polymerase chain reaction) products, complementary or degenerate TaqMan probes were developed. The accuracy of the quantitative real-time PCR (polymerase chain reaction) assay was tested on 3 plant species.

The aim of this study was to evaluate the response to the APT (atopy patch test) with house dust mites (HDM (house dust mites)) in subjects nonaffected by AD (atopic dermatitis) and to compare the outcomes observed in these cases with those pointed out in AD (atopic dermatitis) patients, evaluating also the differences between two allergen extracts manufactured at different purifications and concentrations.
results.reference: The real-time PCR approach revealed promising results in pollen identification and quantification, even when analyzing pollen mixes. Future perspectives could concern the development of multiplex real-time PCR for the simultaneous detection of different taxa in the same reaction tube and the application of high-throughput molecular methods.

results.question: Does diabetes mellitus influence the efficacy of FDG-PET in the diagnosis of cervical cancer?
rewritten_queries: diabetes mellitus effect FDG-PET accuracy cervical cancer diagnosis
impact of hyperglycemia on FDG-PET imaging cervical cancer
diabetes influence PET scan sensitivity specificity cervical cancer
results.answer:
The study described in the abstracts compared the diagnostic ability of FDG-PET in cervical cancer patients with and without diabetes mellitus and found no significant difference in diagnostic power among hyperglycaemic DM, euglycaemic DM, and non-DM groups. Additionally, FDG-PET showed higher detection power than MRI/CT in DM patients, indicating that diabetes mellitus does not negatively influence the efficacy of FDG-PET in diagnosing cervical cancer.

no
contexts: Compared with computed tomography (CT (computed tomography)) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI (magnetic resonance imaging)), positron emission tomography (PET (positron emission tomography)) may have additional value in the assessment of primary and recurrent cervical cancer. However, the degree of tumour uptake of (18)F-2-fluoro-2-deoxy-D: -glucose (FDG (fluoro-2-deoxy-d: -glucose)) uptake is sometimes influenced by diabetes mellitus (DM (diabetes mellitus)). Therefore, we conducted this prospective study to compare the diagnostic ability of FDG (fluoro-2-deoxy-d: -glucose)-PET (positron emission tomography) in patients with cervical cancer complicated by DM (diabetes mellitus) and those without DM (diabetes mellitus).

Patients with untreated locally advanced primary or clinically curable recurrent cervical carcinoma were enrolled. Both FDG (fluoro-2-deoxy-d: -glucose)-PET (positron emission tomography) and MRI (magnetic resonance imaging)/CT (computed tomography) scans were performed within 2 weeks. Patients were categorised into the following groups: hyperglycaemic DM (fasting blood sugar>126 mg/dl), euglycaemic DM (diabetes mellitus) and non-DM (diabetes mellitus). The lesions were confirmed histologically or by clinical follow-up. The receiver operating characteristic curve method, with calculation of the area under the curve (AUC (area under the curve)), was used to evaluate the discriminative power.

From February 2001 to January 2003, 219 patients (75 with primary and 144 with recurrent cervical cancer) were eligible for analysis. Sixteen had hyperglycaemic DM (diabetes mellitus), 12 had euglycaemic DM (diabetes mellitus) and 191 were in the non-DM (diabetes mellitus) group. The diagnostic power of PET (positron emission tomography) in the hyperglycaemic DM (diabetes mellitus), euglycaemic DM (diabetes mellitus) and non-DM (diabetes mellitus) groups did not differ significantly with regard to the identification of either metastatic lesions (AUC (area under the curve), 0.967/0.947/0.925, P>0.05) or primary tumours/local recurrence (AUC (area under the curve), 0.950/0.938/0.979, P>0.05). Considering all DM (diabetes mellitus) patients, PET (positron emission tomography) showed a significantly higher detection power than MRI (magnetic resonance imaging)/CT (computed tomography) scans in respect of metastatic lesions (AUC (area under the curve)=0.956 vs 0.824, P=0.012).

Impaired fasting glucose (IFG (impaired fasting glucose)) below the diagnostic threshold for diabetes mellitus (DM (diabetes mellitus)) is associated with macrovascular pathology and increased mortality after percutaneous coronary interventions. The study goal was to determine whether pre-operative fasting blood glucose (fB-glu) is associated with an increased mortality after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG (coronary artery bypass grafting)).
The effect of neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NACT (neoadjuvant chemotherapy)) on topographical distribution patterns of lymph node metastasis in cervical cancer was unknown.
results.reference: In comparison with its accuracy in non-DM patients, the accuracy of PET in cervical cancer patients with mild to moderate DM was not significantly reduced.

results.question: Biomechanical and wound healing characteristics of corneas after excimer laser keratorefractive surgery: is there a difference between advanced surface ablation and sub-Bowman's keratomileusis?
rewritten_queries: corneal biomechanics excimer laser keratorefractive surgery
wound healing advanced surface ablation vs sub-Bowman's keratomileusis
corneal healing differences surface ablation and sub-Bowman's keratomileusis
results.answer:
The context indicates that advanced surface ablation (ASA) and sub-Bowman's keratomileusis (SBK) differ biomechanically and in wound healing characteristics. ASA reduces some risk of corneal haze compared to PRK but can still develop fibrotic stromal scarring, whereas SBK has potential for interface wound complications due to a hypocellular primitive stromal scar. This suggests distinct differences in their biomechanical safety and wound healing profiles.

yes
contexts: To describe the biomechanical and wound healing characteristics of corneas after excimer laser keratorefractive surgery.

Histologic and ultrastructural studies of normal corneas showed significant differences in the direction of collagen fibrils and/or the degree of lamellar interweaving in Bowman's layer, the anterior third of the corneal stroma, the posterior two-thirds of the corneal stroma, and Descemet's membrane. Cohesive tensile strength testing directly supported these morphologic findings as the stronger, more rigid regions of the cornea were located anteriorly and peripherally. This suggests that PRK (photorefractive keratectomy) and ASA (advanced surface ablation), and secondarily SBK (sub-bowman's keratomileusis), should be biomechanically safer than conventional LASIK with regard to risk for causing keratectasia after surgery. Because adult human corneal stromal wounds heal slowly and incompletely, all excimer laser keratorefractive surgical techniques still have some distinct disadvantages due to inadequate reparative wound healing. Despite reducing some of the risk for corneal haze compared to conventional PRK (photorefractive keratectomy), ASA (advanced surface ablation) cases still can develop corneal haze or breakthrough haze from the hypercellular fibrotic stromal scarring. In contrast, similar to conventional LASIK, SBK (sub-bowman's keratomileusis) still has the short- and long-term potential for interface wound complications from the hypocellular primitive stromal scar.

Histologic, ultrastructural, and cohesive tensile strength evaluations were performed on 25 normal human corneal specimens, 206 uncomplicated LASIK specimens, 17 uncomplicated sub-Bowman's keratomileusis (SBK (sub-bowman's keratomileusis)) specimens, 4 uncomplicated photorefractive keratectomy (PRK (photorefractive keratectomy)) specimens, 2 uncomplicated advanced surface ablation (ASA (advanced surface ablation)) specimens, 5 keratoconus specimens, 12 postoperative LASIK ectasia specimens, and 1 postoperative PRK (photorefractive keratectomy) ectasia specimen and compared to previously published studies.
All patients had extremely fragile, inelastic, and delicate mucosa, which tore easily even with minor trauma. After the procedure, patients remained asymptomatic for 3 to 24 months.

All patients healed their wound properly and no adverse events were recorded. Patients treated conservatively were cured in a mean period of 30 days, while patients treated with CSF drainage were cured in a mean period of 10 days.
results.reference: Ophthalmic pathology and basic science research show that SBK and ASA are improvements in excimer laser keratorefractive surgery compared to conventional LASIK or PRK, particularly with regard to maintaining corneal biomechanics and perhaps moderately reducing the risk of corneal haze. However, most of the disadvantages caused by wound healing issues remain.

results.question: Does radiotherapy of the primary rectal cancer affect prognosis after pelvic exenteration for recurrent rectal cancer?
rewritten_queries: radiotherapy primary rectal cancer prognosis pelvic exenteration recurrent rectal cancer
impact radiotherapy outcomes pelvic exenteration rectal cancer recurrence
results.answer:
The study described in abstracts [1], [2], and [3] shows that patients who received radiotherapy for their primary rectal cancer had worse outcomes after pelvic exenteration for local recurrence, including more radical surgeries, lower rates of clear resection margins, increased surgical complications, and lower disease-free and overall survival. This indicates that radiotherapy of the primary tumor negatively affects prognosis after pelvic exenteration for recurrent rectal cancer.

yes
contexts: This study examined the impact of radiotherapy for the primary rectal cancer on outcomes after pelvic exenteration for local recurrence.

Patients referred for pelvic exenteration from October 1994 to November 2012 were reviewed. Patients who did and did not receive radiotherapy as part of their primary rectal cancer treatment were compared.

There were 108 patients, of which 87 were eligible for analysis. Patients who received radiotherapy for their primary rectal cancer (n = 41) required more radical exenterations (68% vs 44%; p = 0.020), had lower rates of clear resection margins (63% vs 87%; p = 0.010), had increased rates of surgical complications per patient (p = 0.014), and had a lower disease-free survival (p = 0.022). Overall survival and disease-free survival in patients with clear margins were also lower in the primary irradiated patients (p = 0.049 and p<0.0001). This difference in survival persisted in multivariate analysis that corrected for T and N stages of the primary tumor.

A consecutive series of 150 patients with primary rectal cancer were analysed. Fifteen match pairs with open TME (total mesorectal excision) and combined urogenital and anorectal functional assessment at follow up were established identical regarding gender, tumour site, tumour stage, neoadjuvant radiotherapy and type of surgery. Urogenital and anorectal function was evaluated prospectively on the basis of self-administered standardized questionnaires, measurement of residual urine volume and longterm-catheterization rate.

The influence of positron emission tomography in the management of recurrent rectal cancer is well established but its role in primary rectal cancer remains uncertain. This study therefore prospectively assesses the impact of position emission tomography scanning on the management of primary rectal cancer.
results.reference: Patients who previously received radiotherapy for primary rectal cancer treatment have worse oncologic outcomes than those who had not received radiotherapy after pelvic exenteration for locally recurrent rectal cancer.

results.question: Can a practicing surgeon detect early lymphedema reliably?
rewritten_queries: early lymphedema detection clinical signs
reliability of surgeon diagnosis lymphedema
early lymphedema assessment methods clinical practice
results.answer:
The data indicate that detecting early lymphedema using simple circumference measurements has limited sensitivity, with only 37% to 91% detection depending on the criteria used. Since even the best criterion (5% increase at any site) detects 91% of cases, it suggests that a practicing surgeon can detect early lymphedema with reasonable reliability, though not perfectly. Therefore, the evidence supports that early lymphedema can be detected reliably by a practicing surgeon using circumference changes.

yes
contexts: Ninety breast cancer patients were prospectively enrolled in an academic trial, and seven upper extremity circumferences were measured quarterly for 3 years. A 10% volume increase or greater than 1 cm increase in arm circumference identified lymphedema with verification by a lymphedema specialist. Sensitivity and specificity of several different criteria for detecting lymphedema were compared using the academic trial as the standard.

Thirty-nine cases of lymphedema were identified by the academic trial. Using a 10% increase in circumference at two sites as the criterion, half the lymphedema cases were detected (sensitivity 37%). When using a 10% increase in circumference at any site, 74.4% of cases were detected (sensitivity 49%). Detection by a 5% increase in circumference at any site was 91% sensitive.

Among 2,027 consecutive SLN (sentinel lymph node) biopsy procedures performed by two experienced surgeons, clinically suspicious axillary nodes were identified in 106, and categorized as group 1 (asymmetric enlargement of the ipsilateral axillary nodes moderately suspicious for metastasis, n = 62) and group 2 (clinically positive axillary nodes highly suspicious for metastasis, n = 44).
Lymphedema may be identified by simpler circumference changes as compared with changes in limb volume.

Thirty-five (12.4%) of 282 patients had recurrence in vaginal vault, 51 patients (18.0%) had recurrence in central pelvis, 14 patients (4.9%) had recurrence in pelvic wall, and 39 patients (13.8%) had recurrence in lymph nodes. One-hundred twenty-eight patients (45.3%) showed a distant relapse, whereas 15 patients (5.3%) developed both distant relapse and local relapse. The site of relapse influenced survival because the patients with vaginal vault recurrences lived significantly longer than the patients with recurrences in other sites. Eighty (28.4%) of the 282 patients became symptomatic and anticipated the scheduled visit, 37 (13.1 %) of the patients reported their symptoms during the follow-up meeting, and 165 (58.5 %) of the patients were asymptomatic and the diagnostic path was introduced by a planned visit or examination. Among the asymptomatic patients, the first procedure that led to further examinations was clinical visit alone for 60 (36.4%) of 165 patients, imaging for 103 patients (62.4%), and cytologic examination for 2 patients (1.2%). Symptoms at recurrence can predict survival: patients with an asymptomatic recurrence had a median survival time from relapse of 35 months versus 13 months if they had a symptomatic repetition (P = 0.0001).
results.reference: An increase of 5% in circumference measurements identified the most potential lymphedema cases compared with an academic trial.

results.question: Colorectal cancer with synchronous liver metastases: does global management at the same centre improve results?
rewritten_queries: colorectal cancer synchronous liver metastases multidisciplinary management outcomes
colorectal cancer liver metastases treatment centralized care impact survival
results.answer:
The data show that overall survival rates at 3 and 5 years were not significantly different between global management (GM) and separate management (SM) groups. Additionally, disease-free survival at 5 years was actually higher in the SM group (14% vs. 11%, P = 0.009). Therefore, global management at the same centre does not appear to improve results compared to separate management.

no
contexts: Synchronous liver metastases (SLM (synchronous liver metastases)) occur in 20% of colorectal cancers (CRC (colorectal cancers)). Resection of SLM (synchronous liver metastases) and CLC can be undertaken at different centres (separate management, SM) or at the same centre (global management, GM).
Retrospective study of SLM (synchronous liver metastases) and CRC (colorectal cancers) resections carried out during 01/2000 - 12/2006 by SM or GM, using a combined or delayed strategy.

Morphologic characteristics and type of CRC (colorectal cancers) and SLM (synchronous liver metastases) resection were similar for the GM (n = 45) or SM (n = 66) groups. In patients with delayed liver resection (62 SM, 17 GM), chemotherapy prior to liver surgery was used in 92% and 38% of SM and GM patients (P<0.0001) and the median delay between procedures was 212 and 182 days, respectively (P = 0.04). First step of liver resection was more often performed during colorectal surgery in the GM group (62 vs. 6% for SM, P<0.0001) and the mean number of procedures (CRC (colorectal cancers)+SLM (synchronous liver metastases)) was lower (1.6 vs. 2.3, P = 0.003). Three-month mortality was 3% for GM and 0% for SM (n.s.). Overall survival rates were 67% and 51% for SM and GM at 3 years (n.s.), and 35 and 31% at 5 years (n.s.). Disease-free survival to 5 years was higher in SM patients (14% vs. 11%, P = 0.009).

The presence of metastases correlated with the downregulation of TCR zeta, especially CD8(+) T cells. The most striking feature was the reduction in the number of myeloid CD11c(+) dendritic cells in the LN of patients with LN metastases. This could be a reflection of the immunodeficient state observed in lung cancer patients. Even in the absence of metastases in the regional LN, the same type of changes in the LN microenvironment were observed in those LN located nearer the primary tumor.

This was a single-center, retrospective cohort study which included patients diagnosed with colorectal cancer at age ≤40 years in 1997-2013 matched 1:2 by year of diagnosis with consecutive colorectal cancer patients diagnosed at age>50 years during the same period. Patients aged 41-50 years were not included in the study, to accentuate potential age-related differences. Clinicopathological characteristics, treatment, and outcome were compared between groups.
results.reference: GM of CRC and SLM was associated with fewer procedures but did not influence overall survival. Significant differences or correlations between hormone receptor expression (oestrogen and progesterone) and cell growth indices (Ki67 and Bcl-2).

A prerequisite for a hormonal influence on anal continence in women is the presence of hormone receptors in the tissues of the anal canal. results.reference: In the present study, FT and androstenedione were statistically significantly correlated with sexual desire in the total cohort of women. Vaginal intraepithelial neoplasia is a little known disease which could be related to risk factors different from simple HPV infections.

contexts: To determine the impact of PRISM on LOS (length of picu stay), and evaluate an Artificial Neural Network's (ANN (artificial neural network's)) performance to estimate LOS (length of picu stay) from PRISM item patterns.

Retrospectively we performed correlation and regression analyses on routinely scored PRISM data of all consecutive admissions to our level-III PICU (pediatric intensive care unit) from 1994 to 1999 (n>2000) with individual LOS (length of picu stay). 204 children were recruited in the main cohort and 97 in the replication cohort. The number of detected viruses did not correlate with any markers of severity. In addition, pneumococcal vaccination was found to be a protective factor in terms of degree of respiratory distress (OR: 2.917; P-value = 0.035), PICU (pediatric intensive care unit) admission (OR: 0.301; P-value = 0.011), lower clinical score (-1.499; P-value = 0.021) respiratory support requirement (OR: 0.324; P-value = 0.016) and oxygen necessity (OR: 0.328; P-value = 0.001). All these findings were replicated in the UK cohort.
results.reference: The ANN with its intrinsic ability to detect non-linear correlation, and to relate specific item patterns to LOS, outperformed linear statistics but was still disappointing in estimating individual LOS. It might be speculated that therapeutic intervention modulates the natural course of the disease thus counteracting both disease severity as initially scored by PRISM, and LOS. This being true, the inverse of the correlation between PRISM (or PRISM based LOS estimate) and LOS might be a candidate indicator of quality of care.

Aortoplasty was associated with aortic valve replacement in 47 cases (35 mechanical vs 12 biological), subvalvular myectomy in 29 cases, and CABG (coronary artery bypass graft) in 13 cases. It was the aim of the present study to elaborate criteria for the assessment of rapid hemodynamic progression of valvar aortic stenosis. results.answer:

Inept practitioners can miscalculate the danger and lose their gamble with death, implying that while it is pursued for secret pleasure, it can result in lethal outcomes.

contexts: Voluntary asphyxiation among children, preteens, and adolescents by hanging or other means of inducing hypoxia/anoxia to enhance sexual excitement is not uncommon and can lead to unintended death. This study addresses autoerotic asphyxiation (AEA (autoerotic asphyxiation)) with the intent of increasing pediatricians' knowledge of the syndrome and awareness of its typical onset among young patients. AEA (autoerotic asphyxiation) is characteristically a clandestine and elusive practice. Provided with relevant information, pediatricians can identify the syndrome, demonstrate a willingness to discuss concerns about it, ameliorate distress, and possibly prevent a tragedy.

AEA (autoerotic asphyxiation) can be conceptualized as a personalized, ritualized, and symbolic biopsychosocial drama. It seems to be a reenactment of intense emotional feeling-states involving an identification and sadomasochistic relationship with a female figure. Inept AEA (autoerotic asphyxiation) practitioners can miscalculate the peril of the situation that they have contrived and for numerous reasons lose their gamble with death.

A retrospective study was undertaken of published cases both fatal and nonfatal and included personal communications, referenced citations, clinical experience, and theoretical formulations as to causation. Characteristic AEA (autoerotic asphyxiation) manifestations, prevalence, age range, methods of inducing hypoxia/anoxia, and gender weighting are presented. A total of 103 carotid endarterectomies were performed in 95 octogenarians. Procedures were performed on 59 men and 36 women. There were 4 perioperative neurologic complications, which included 1 transient ischemic attack (0.97%), 2 minor strokes (1.94%), and 1 major stroke (0.97%). There were no deaths.

Uncontrolled hemorrhage is the leading cause of fatality. The aim of this study was to evaluate the effect of zeolite mineral (QuikClot - Advanced Clotting Sponge [QC-ACS]) on blood loss and physiological variables in a swine extremity arterial injury model.
results.reference: Pediatricians should be alert to the earliest manifestations of AEA. Awareness of choking games among the young and, of those, a subset who eventually progress to potentially fatal AEA is strongly encouraged among all primary care professionals who may be able to interrupt the behavior.

results.answer:

This suggests that while comorbidity is initially associated with poorer depression outcomes, this effect may be explained by other factors.

Longitudinal data were used to model associations between a four-level classification of MD (major depression)/AUD (alcohol use disorder) during the period 15-18 years (neither; MD (major depression)-only; AUD (alcohol use disorder)-only; comorbid MD (major depression)/AUD (alcohol use disorder)) and MD (major depression) over the period 18-35 years. The three disorder groups had rates of adult MD (major depression) during the period 18-35 years that were significantly (p<.05) higher than that of the group with no disorder. Furthermore, those in the comorbid MD (major depression)/AUD (alcohol use disorder) group had significantly (p<.05) higher rates of adult MD (major depression) than those in the AUD (alcohol use disorder)-only group, and marginally (p<.10) higher rates of adult MD (major depression) than those in the MD (major depression)-only group. After adjustment for confounding, the difference in rates of adult MD (major depression) between the MD (major depression)-only group and the MD (major depression)/AUD (alcohol use disorder) group were no longer statistically significant. To explore the extent to which parent-adolescent emotional closeness, family conflict, and parental permissiveness moderate the association of puberty and alcohol use in adolescents (aged 10-14).

Cross-sectional survey of 7631 adolescents from 231 Australian schools. Measures included pubertal status, recent (30day) alcohol use, parent-adolescent emotional closeness, family conflict, parental permissiveness of alcohol use and peer alcohol use. The analysis was based on a two-level (individuals nested within schools) logistic regression model, with main effects entered first, and interaction terms added second.
results.reference: The results of these analyses suggest that marginally higher rates of depression to age 35 amongst the comorbid MD/AUD group were explained by increased exposure to adverse childhood circumstances amongst members of the comorbid group. results.question: Does a 4 diagram manual enable laypersons to operate the Laryngeal Mask Supreme®?
rewritten_queries: Laryngeal Mask Supreme® user manual layperson usability
Laryngeal Mask Supreme® 4 diagram instruction effectiveness
layperson ability to use Laryngeal Mask Supreme® with simplified manual
results.answer:
The study described in abstracts [1], [2], and [3] shows that laypersons were able to use a 4-diagram instruction manual to operate the Laryngeal Mask Supreme® on a manikin, with 96.7% inserting it correctly and 79.3% successfully providing ventilation within 2 minutes. This indicates that the manual effectively enables laypersons to operate the device.

yes
contexts: Bystander resuscitation plays an important role in lifesaving cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR (cardiopulmonary resuscitation)). A significant reduction in the "no-flow-time", quantitatively better chest compressions and an improved quality of ventilation can be demonstrated during CPR (cardiopulmonary resuscitation) using supraglottic airway devices (SADs (supraglottic airway devices)). Previous studies have demonstrated the ability of inexperienced persons to operate SADs (supraglottic airway devices) after brief instruction. The aim of this pilot study was to determine whether an instruction manual consisting of four diagrams enables laypersons to operate a Laryngeal Mask Supreme® (LMAS (laryngeal mask supreme®)) in the manikin.

An instruction manual of four illustrations with speech bubbles displaying the correct use of the LMAS (laryngeal mask supreme®) was designed. Laypersons were handed a bag containing a LMAS (laryngeal mask supreme®), a bag mask valve device (BMV (bag mask valve device)), a syringe prefilled with air and the instruction sheet, and were asked to perform and ventilate the manikin as displayed. Time to ventilation was recorded and degree of success evaluated.

A total of 150 laypersons took part. Overall 145 participants (96.7%) inserted the LMAS (laryngeal mask supreme®) in the manikin in the right direction. The device was inserted inverted or twisted in 13 (8.7%) attempts. Eight (5.3%) individuals recognized this and corrected the position. Within the first 2 minutes 119 (79.3%) applicants were able to insert the LMAS (laryngeal mask supreme®) and provide tidal volumes greater than 150 ml (estimated dead space). Time to insertion and first ventilation was 83.2 ± 29 s. No significant difference related to previous BLS training (P = 0.85), technical education (P = 0.07) or gender could be demonstrated (P = 0.25).

Using a patient simulator of a head and thorax that was able to record respiratory rate, tidal volume, peak pressure, and minute volume via a laptop computer, participants were asked to ventilate the simulator during six 1-minute ventilation tests. The first scenario was BVM (bag-valve-mask) ventilation with an oropharyngeal airway in place ventilating with both an adult- and pediatric-sized BVM (bag-valve-mask), the second scenario had a supraglottic airway and both bags, and the third scenario had an endotracheal tube and both bags. Participants were enrolled in convenience manner while they were on-duty and the research staff was able to travel to their stations. Prior to enrolling, participants were not given any additional training on ventilation skills.

114 individuals trained in basic life support and bag-valve-mask ventilation participated in this study. Individual characteristics were obtained by the observer and the education and practice level were described by the subjects. Ventilation was delivered with a manual resuscitator connected to a microspirometer and volumes were measured. Subjects completed three procedures: one-handed, two-handed and two-handed half-compression.
results.reference: In manikin laypersons could insert LMAS in the correct direction after onsite instruction by a simple manual with a high success rate. This indicates some basic procedural understanding and intellectual transfer in principle. Operating errors (n = 91) were frequently not recognized and corrected (n = 77). Improvements in labeling and the quality of instructional photographs may reduce individual error and may optimize understanding.

We determined the agreement of SLBM (slit-lamp biomicroscopy-based method) and CIP (colvard infrared pupillometry), intraobserver and interobserver repeatabilities, and interobserver concordance (kappa) and SLBM (slit-lamp biomicroscopy-based method) ability for detecting pupil sizes over 6.0 mm.

The aim of this prospective, randomized study was to compare the hemodynamic performance of the Medtronic Mosaic and Edwards Perimount bioprostheses in the aortic position, and to evaluate prosthesis-specific differences in valve sizing and valve-size labeling.

Therefore, paucigranulocytic asthma cannot be considered truly non-inflammatory based on these findings.

no
contexts: The technique of induced sputum has allowed to subdivide asthma patients into inflammatory phenotypes according to their level of granulocyte airway infiltration. There are very few studies which looked at detailed sputum and blood cell counts in a large cohort of asthmatics divided into inflammatory phenotypes. The purpose of this study was to analyze sputum cell counts, blood leukocytes and systemic inflammatory markers in these phenotypes, and investigate how those groups compared with healthy subjects.

The total non-squamous cell count per gram of sputum was greater in mixed granulocytic and neutrophilic phenotypes as compared to eosinophilic, paucigranulocytic asthma and healthy subjects (p < 0.005). Sputum eosinophils (in absolute values and percentages) were increased in all asthma phenotypes including paucigranulocytic asthma, compared to healthy subjects (p < 0.005). Eosinophilic asthma showed higher absolute sputum neutrophil and lymphocyte counts than healthy subjects (p < 0.005), while neutrophilic asthmatics had a particularly low number of sputum macrophages and epithelial cells. All asthma phenotypes showed an increased blood leukocyte count compared to healthy subjects (p < 0.005), with paucigranulocytic asthmatics having also increased absolute blood eosinophils compared to healthy subjects (p < 0.005). Neutrophilic asthma had raised CRP (C reactive protein) and fibrinogen while eosinophilic asthma only showed raised fibrinogen compared to healthy subjects (p < 0.005).

We conducted a retrospective cross-sectional study on 833 asthmatics recruited from the University Asthma Clinic of Liege and compared them with 194 healthy subjects. Asthmatics were classified into inflammatory phenotypes.

We studied 100 asthma patients who were divided into the following four groups: patients with obstruction who were either ICS-naive (group I) or were treated with ICSs (group II (group i) or were treated with icss)); and nonobstructed patients who were either ICS-naive (group III) or were treated with ICSs (group IV). PD (perception of dyspnea) on the visual analog scale (VAS (visual analog scale)) was assessed during a methacholine-induced FEV(1) decrease and specifically was quantified as the VAS (visual analog scale) slope and score at an FEV(1) decrease of 5 to 20%. BHR (bronchial hyperresponsiveness) was assessed in terms of the provocative concentration of methacholine causing a 20% fall in FEV(1) (PC(20)). Eosinophil counts in induced sputum samples also were performed. Regression analysis, univariate analysis of variance, and factor analysis were applied for statistical evaluation.

Some of the disagreements on the perception of dyspnea (PD (perception of dyspnea)) during bronchoconstriction in asthma patients could depend on the interrelationships among the following: (1) the influence of baseline airflow obstruction on the patient's ability to detect any further increase in airway resistance; (2) the effect of eosinophilic inflammation on the airway; (3) bronchial hyperresponsiveness (BHR (bronchial hyperresponsiveness)); and (4) the effect of inhaled corticosteroids (ICSs (inhaled corticosteroids)).
results.reference: This study demonstrates that a significant eosinophilic inflammation is present across all categories of asthma, and that paucigranulocytic asthma may be seen as a low grade inflammatory disease.

results.question: Is HIV/STD control in Jamaica making a difference?
rewritten_queries: HIV STD control Jamaica effectiveness
HIV prevention programs Jamaica impact
sexually transmitted infections prevalence Jamaica recent data
results.answer:
The data from Jamaica show that the HIV/AIDS incidence rate increased only marginally over three years, while HIV prevalence in the general population remained low (about 1% or less). Additionally, there were significant increases in condom use and declines in syphilis rates and congenital syphilis cases, indicating positive behavioral changes and disease control. These findings suggest that the comprehensive HIV/STD Control Program in Jamaica is having a beneficial impact.

yes
contexts: To assess the impact of the comprehensive HIV (human immunodeficiency virus)/STD (sexually transmitted disease) Control Program established in Jamaica since the late 1980s on the HIV (human immunodeficiency virus)/AIDS (acquired immunodeficiency syndrome) epidemic.

The annual AIDS (acquired immunodeficiency syndrome) incidence rate in Jamaica increased only marginally in the past three years from 18.5 per 100000 population to 21.4 in 1997. HIV (human immunodeficiency virus) prevalence in the general population groups tested has been about 1% or less. Among those at high risk, HIV (human immunodeficiency virus) prevalence rates have risen to 6.3% (95% confidence interval 5.0-8.0) in STD (sexually transmitted disease) clinic attenders, around 10% and 21% in female prostitutes in Kingston and Montego Bay respectively and approximately 30% among homosexuals. Syphilis rates and congenital syphilis cases have declined. The proportion of men aged 15-49 years reporting sex with a non-regular partner declined from 35% in 1994 to 26% in 1996 (P<0.001). Women ever having used condoms increased from 51% in 1988 to 62.5% in 1992 and 73% in 1994 and 1996 (P<0.001), while condom use with a non-regular partner increased from 37% in 1992 to 73% in 1996 (P= 0.006). Condom use among men was high over the period: around 81% had ever used condoms and 77% used them with non-regular partners. Gay men, inner-city adults and adolescents aged 12-14 years all reported increases in condom use while condom sales and distribution increased from around 2 million in 1985 to 10 million in 1995.

AIDS (acquired immunodeficiency syndrome) case reports, HIV (human immunodeficiency virus) testing of blood donors, antenatal clinic attenders (ANC (antenatal clinic attenders)), food service workers, sexually transmitted disease (STD (sexually transmitted disease)) clinic attenders, female prostitutes, homosexuals and other groups were used to monitor the HIV (human immunodeficiency virus)/AIDS (acquired immunodeficiency syndrome) epidemic. Primary and secondary syphilis and cases of congenital syphilis were also monitored. National knowledge, attitude and practice (KAP (knowledge, attitude and practice)) surveys were conducted in 1988, 1989, 1992, 1994 and 1996.

MMR (maternal mortality ratio) ranged from 10 per 100,000 (the Netherlands) to 1540 per 100,000 (The Gambia). Differences in causes of deaths were characterized by HIV (human immunodeficiency virus)/AIDS (acquired immunodeficiency syndrome) in Namibia, sepsis and HIV (human immunodeficiency virus)/AIDS (acquired immunodeficiency syndrome) in Zambia, (pre-)eclampsia in the Netherlands and obstructed labour in The Gambia.
To evaluate whether reported unsafe sexual behaviour among HIV (human immunodeficiency virus)- infected individuals is changing over time.
results.reference: HIV/STD control measures appear to have slowed the HIV/AIDS epidemic in Jamaica, however a significant minority of persons continue to have unprotected sex in high risk situations.

results.question: Is Panton-Valentine leucocidin associated with the pathogenesis of Staphylococcus aureus bacteraemia in the UK?
rewritten_queries: Panton-Valentine leucocidin Staphylococcus aureus bacteraemia pathogenesis UK
PVL toxin role Staphylococcus aureus bloodstream infection United Kingdom
results.answer:
The data show that only a very small proportion (1.6%) of Staphylococcus aureus bacteraemia isolates in the UK and Ireland were PVL-positive, and these were methicillin-susceptible strains. No PVL-positive isolates were methicillin-resistant, and the clinical details do not establish a clear role of PVL in the pathogenesis of bacteraemia. Therefore, the evidence does not support a significant association of PVL with the pathogenesis of S. aureus bacteraemia in the UK.

no
contexts: The morbidity and mortality associated with Panton-Valentine leucocidin (PVL (panton-valentine leucocidin))-positive Staphylococcus aureus suggest that this toxin is a key marker of disease severity. Nevertheless, the importance of PVL (panton-valentine leucocidin) in the pathogenesis of primary bacteraemia caused by S. aureus is uncertain. We have determined the prevalence of PVL (panton-valentine leucocidin)-encoding genes among isolates of S. aureus from bacteraemic patients.

Consecutive bacteraemia isolates of S. aureus (n=244) from patients hospitalized in 25 centres in the UK and Ireland during 2005 were screened for PVL (panton-valentine leucocidin) and mecA genes. PVL (panton-valentine leucocidin)-positive isolates were characterized by toxin gene profiling, PFGE, spa-typing and MIC determinations for a range of antimicrobials.

Four out of 244 isolates (1.6%) were PVL (panton-valentine leucocidin)-positive and susceptible to oxacillin [methicillin-susceptible S. aureus (MSSA)]. Eighty-eight out of 244 (36%) were oxacillin-resistant (methicillin-resistant S. aureus), but none was PVL (panton-valentine leucocidin)-positive. The four patients (two males: 30 and 33 years; two females: 62 and 80 years) had infection foci of: skin and soft tissue, unknown, indwelling line, and surgical site, and were located at one centre in Wales, one in England and two in Ireland. One of four PVL (panton-valentine leucocidin)-positive isolates was resistant to penicillin and fusidic acid, the remainder were susceptible to all antibiotics tested. Genotypic analyses showed that the four isolates represented three distinct strains; the two isolates from Ireland were related.

HCC (hexamidine-chlorhexidine-chlorocresol) did not present any bactericidal activity except on P. aeruginosa at a concentration of 97%. P was not bactericidal on E. hirae at any concentration and on S. aureus at 97%. CB (chlorhexidine-benzalkonium) had the most homogeneous bactericidal activity with a reduction>5 log on the 4 bacterial strains at concentrations of 97%, 50% and 10%.

204 children were recruited in the main cohort and 97 in the replication cohort. The number of detected viruses did not correlate with any markers of severity. However, bacterial superinfection was associated with increased severity (OR: 4.356; P-value = 0.005), PICU (pediatric intensive care unit) admission (OR: 3.342; P-value = 0.006), higher clinical score (1.988; P-value = 0.002) respiratory support requirement (OR: 7.484; P-value<0.001) and longer hospital length of stay (OR: 1.468; P-value<0.001). In addition, pneumococcal vaccination was found to be a protective factor in terms of degree of respiratory distress (OR: 2.917; P-value = 0.035), PICU (pediatric intensive care unit) admission (OR: 0.301; P-value = 0.011), lower clinical score (-1.499; P-value = 0.021) respiratory support requirement (OR: 0.324; P-value = 0.016) and oxygen necessity (OR: 0.328; P-value = 0.001). All these findings were replicated in the UK cohort.
results.reference: We found that 1.6% of S. aureus (all MSSA) from bacteraemic patients were PVL-positive. This low incidence suggests that PVL-positive S. aureus are of no particular significance as causative agents of S. aureus bacteraemia.

results.question: Are even impaired fasting blood glucose levels preoperatively associated with increased mortality after CABG surgery?

fasting blood glucose levels cardiac surgery outcomes
preoperative hyperglycemia mortality coronary artery bypass graft
results.answer:
The study in abstract [3] shows that non-diabetics with impaired fasting glucose (IFG) had a relative risk of 1.7 for 30-day mortality and 2.9 for 1-year mortality after CABG compared to those with normal fasting glucose, indicating an increased mortality risk associated with IFG. Although confidence intervals are wide, the receiver operator characteristic area for fasting glucose and 1-year mortality was statistically significant (P=0.002), supporting the association between even impaired fasting glucose levels and increased mortality after CABG.

yes
contexts: Impaired fasting glucose (IFG (impaired fasting glucose)) below the diagnostic threshold for diabetes mellitus (DM (diabetes mellitus)) is associated with macrovascular pathology and increased mortality after percutaneous coronary interventions. The study goal was to determine whether pre-operative fasting blood glucose (fB-glu) is associated with an increased mortality after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG (coronary artery bypass grafting)).

The anesthetical-surgical procedure presented a mortality rate of 3.125% (1:32) and a morbidity rate of 6.25% (2:32). It was evidenced an initial mean blood glucose = 199.4 mg/dl and the end = 326.1 mg/dl. In spite of extended fasting (minimum of 2 hours for the absolute fasting and maximum of 8.5 hours for liquids, and 20.5 hours for solids) all animals presented at the end of the surgical procedure any gastric content and a blood glucose increase. Those with fasting for liquids and solids when compared to the quantity of solid gastric content, presented a moderate negative degree of correlation.

During 2001-03, 1895 patients underwent primary CABG (coronary artery bypass grafting) [clinical DM (CDM (clinical dm)) in 440/1895; complete data on fB-glu for n=1375/1455]. Using pre-operative fB-glu, non-diabetics were categorized as having normal fB-glu (<5.6 mmol/L), IFG (5.6<or =fB-glu<6.1 mmol/L), or suspected DM (SDM (suspected dm)) (>or =6.1 mmol/L). fB-glu was normal in 59%. The relative risks of 30 day and 1 year mortality compared with patients with normal fB-glu was 1.7 [95% confidence interval (CI (confidence interval)): 0.5-5.5] and 2.9 (CI (confidence interval): 0.8-11.2) with IFG (impaired fasting glucose), 2.8 (CI (confidence interval): 1.1-7.2) and 1.9 (CI (confidence interval): 0.5-6.3) with SDM (suspected dm) vs. 1.8 (CI (confidence interval): 0.8-4.0) and 1.6 (CI (confidence interval): 0.6-4.3) if CDM (clinical dm), respectively. The receiver operator characteristic area for the continuous variable fB-glu and 1 year mortality was 0.65 (P=0.002).

A total of 12 537 participants with dysglycaemia and high CV (cardiovascular)-risk were randomized to basal insulin glargine titrated to a fasting glucose of ≤ 5.3 mmol/L (95 mg/dL) or standard glycaemic care. Non-severe hypoglycaemia was defined as symptoms confirmed by glucose ≤ 54 mg/dL and severe hypoglycaemia as a requirement for assistance or glucose ≤ 36 mg/dL. Outcomes were: (i) the composite of CV (cardiovascular) death, non-fatal myocardial infarction or stroke; (ii) mortality; (iii) CV (cardiovascular) mortality; and (iv) arrhythmic death. Hazards were estimated before and after adjustment for a hypoglycaemia propensity score. During a median of 6.2 years (IQR: 5.8-6.7), non-severe hypoglycaemic episodes occurred in 41.7 and 14.4% glargine and standard group participants, respectively, while severe episodes occurred in 5.7 and 1.8%, respectively. Non-severe hypoglycaemia was not associated with any outcome following adjustment. Conversely, severe hypoglycaemia was associated with a greater risk for the primary outcome (HR: 1.58; 95% CI (confidence interval): 1.24-2.02, P<0.001), mortality (HR: 1.74; 95% CI (confidence interval): 1.39-2.19, P<0.001), CV (cardiovascular) death (HR: 1.71; 95% CI (confidence interval): 1.27-2.30, P<0.001) and arrhythmic death (HR: 1.77; 95% CI (confidence interval): 1.17-2.67, P = 0.007). Similar findings were noted for severe nocturnal hypoglycaemia for the primary outcome and mortality. The severe hypoglycaemia hazard for all four outcomes was higher with standard care than with insulin glargine.

The overall incidence of postoperative AF (atrial fibrillation) was 26%. Postoperative AF (atrial fibrillation) was significantly lower in the Statin group compared with the Non-statin group (16% versus 33%, p = 0.005). Multivariate analysis demonstrated that independent predictors of AF (atrial fibrillation) development after CABG (coronary artery bypass grafting) were preoperative statin therapy (odds ratio [OR]0.327, 95% confidence interval [CI (confidence interval)] 0.107 to 0.998, p = 0.05) and age (OR 1.058, 95% CI (confidence interval) 1.004 to 1.116, p = 0.035).
results.reference: The elevated risk of death after CABG surgery known previously to be associated with CDM seems also to be shared by a group of similar size that includes patients with IFG and undiagnosed DM.

results.question: Does positron emission tomography change management in primary rectal cancer?
rewritten_queries: positron emission tomography impact treatment decisions primary rectal cancer
PET scan management changes rectal cancer staging
role of PET in primary rectal cancer therapy planning
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that positron emission tomography (PET) scanning changed the management in 17% of patients with primary rectal cancer, including cancellation of surgery and changes in radiotherapy fields. Additionally, PET altered the overall tumor stage in 39% of patients, and follow-up confirmed the appropriateness of these PET-induced management changes. Therefore, PET does influence management decisions in primary rectal cancer.

yes
contexts: The influence of positron emission tomography in the management of recurrent rectal cancer is well established but its role in primary rectal cancer remains uncertain. This study therefore prospectively assesses the impact of position emission tomography scanning on the management of primary rectal cancer.

Forty-six patients with advanced primary rectal cancer referred for consideration of adjuvant preoperative therapy underwent position emission tomography scanning. The referring physicians prospectively recorded each patient's stage following conventional imaging and the proposed treatment plan prior to position emission tomography scanning. This was then compared with subsequent stage and actual management implemented, and the appropriateness of position emission tomography-induced changes was noted by subsequent clinical follow-up.

Compared with computed tomography (CT (computed tomography)) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI (magnetic resonance imaging)), positron emission tomography (PET (positron emission tomography)) may have additional value in the assessment of primary and recurrent cervical cancer. However, the degree of tumour uptake of (18)F-2-fluoro-2-deoxy-D: -glucose (FDG (fluoro-2-deoxy-d: -glucose)) uptake is sometimes influenced by diabetes mellitus (DM (diabetes mellitus)). Therefore, we conducted this prospective study to compare the diagnostic ability of FDG (fluoro-2-deoxy-d: -glucose)-PET (positron emission tomography) in patients with cervical cancer complicated by DM (diabetes mellitus) and those without DM (diabetes mellitus).

The surgical management of 36 of 46 patients (78 percent) was unchanged as a result of position emission tomography, even though position emission tomography upstaged disease in 3 of 36 cases (8 percent) and downstaged disease in 5 of 36 cases (14 percent). In 8 of 46 cases (17 percent), management was altered because of the position emission tomography scan findings, including 6 cases (13 percent) in which surgery was cancelled and 2 other cases (4 percent) in which the radiotherapy field was changed. Where available, follow-up confirmed the appropriateness of position emission tomography-induced management change in each case. Two patients had a change in therapy independent of the position emission tomography scan due to clinical circumstances. Overall tumor stage was changed following position emission tomography in 18 of 46 patients (39 percent).

From February 2001 to January 2003, 219 patients (75 with primary and 144 with recurrent cervical cancer) were eligible for analysis. Sixteen had hyperglycaemic DM (diabetes mellitus), 12 had euglycaemic DM (diabetes mellitus) and 191 were in the non-DM (diabetes mellitus) group. The diagnostic power of PET (positron emission tomography) in the hyperglycaemic DM (diabetes mellitus), euglycaemic DM (diabetes mellitus) and non-DM (diabetes mellitus) groups did not differ significantly with regard to the identification of either metastatic lesions (AUC (area under the curve), 0.967/0.947/0.925, P>0.05) or primary tumours/local recurrence (AUC (area under the curve), 0.950/0.938/0.979, P>0.05). Considering all DM (diabetes mellitus) patients, PET (positron emission tomography) showed a significantly higher detection power than MRI (magnetic resonance imaging)/CT (computed tomography) scans in respect of metastatic lesions (AUC (area under the curve)=0.956 vs 0.824, P=0.012).
results.reference: Position emission tomography scanning appears to accurately change the stage or appropriately alter the therapy of almost a third of patients with advanced primary rectal cancer. In view of this, we suggest that position emission tomography scanning be considered part of standard workup for such patients, particularly if neoadjuvant chemoradiation is being considered as part of primary management.

results.question: Can you deliver accurate tidal volume by manual resuscitator?
rewritten_queries: manual resuscitator tidal volume accuracy
manual ventilation tidal volume control
manual resuscitator volume delivery reliability
results.answer:
The studies indicate that tidal volumes delivered by manual resuscitators vary depending on the method used (one-handed vs. two-handed) and the type of device (pediatric vs. adult BVM), with two-handed methods generally delivering higher volumes. Although physical characteristics and education/practice levels have weak correlations with volume accuracy, the pediatric BVM was more likely to deliver tidal volumes within the recommended range. This suggests that accurate tidal volume delivery by manual resuscitator is achievable but can be influenced by technique and device choice.

yes
contexts: One of the problems with manual resuscitators is the difficulty in achieving accurate volume delivery. The volume delivered to the patient varies by the physical characteristics of the person and method. This study was designed to compare tidal volumes delivered by the squeezing method, physical characteristics and education and practice levels.

The mean (standard deviation) volumes for the one-handed method were 592.84 ml (SD 117.39), two-handed 644.24 ml (SD 144.7) and two-handed half-compression 458.31 ml (SD 120.91) (p<0.01). Tidal volume delivered by two hands was significantly greater than that delivered by one hand (r = 0.398, p<0.01). The physical aspects including hand size, volume and grip power had no correlation with the volume delivered. There were slight increases in tidal volume with education and practice, but correlation was weak (r = 0.213, r = 0.281, r = 0.131, p<0.01).

114 individuals trained in basic life support and bag-valve-mask ventilation participated in this study. Individual characteristics were obtained by the observer and the education and practice level were described by the subjects. Ventilation was delivered with a manual resuscitator connected to a microspirometer and volumes were measured. Subjects completed three procedures: one-handed, two-handed and two-handed half-compression.

We enrolled 50 providers from a large, busy, urban fire-based EMS (emergency medical services) agency with 14.96 (SD = 9.92) mean years of experience. Only 1.5% of all breaths delivered with the pediatric BVM (bag-valve-mask) during the ventilation scenarios were below the recommended tidal volume. A greater percentage of breaths delivered in the recommended range occurred when the pediatric BVM (bag-valve-mask) was used (17.5% vs 5.1%, p<0.001). Median volumes for each scenario were 570.5mL, 664.0mL, 663.0mL for the pediatric BMV and 796.0mL, 994.5mL, 981.5mL for the adult BVM (bag-valve-mask). In all three categories of airway devices, the pediatric BVM (bag-valve-mask) provided lower median tidal volumes (p<0.001).

A total of 150 laypersons took part. Overall 145 participants (96.7%) inserted the LMAS (laryngeal mask supreme®) in the manikin in the right direction. The device was inserted inverted or twisted in 13 (8.7%) attempts. Eight (5.3%) individuals recognized this and corrected the position. Within the first 2 minutes 119 (79.3%) applicants were able to insert the LMAS (laryngeal mask supreme®) and provide tidal volumes greater than 150 ml (estimated dead space). Time to insertion and first ventilation was 83.2 ± 29 s. No significant difference related to previous BLS training (P = 0.85), technical education (P = 0.07) or gender could be demonstrated (P = 0.25).
results.reference: The tidal volume delivered by a manual resuscitator shows large variations. There were significant differences in the volume delivered by compression methods, but physical characteristics are not a predictor of tidal volume delivery. The manual resuscitator is not a suitable device for accurate ventilation.

results.question: Can increases in the cigarette tax rate be linked to cigarette retail prices?

no
contexts: The 2009 excise tax increase on cigarettes in China has not translated into higher retail prices because the Chinese STMA (state tobacco monopoly administration) used its policy authority to ensure that retail cigarette prices did not change. The government tax increase is being collected at both the producer and wholesale levels. As a result, the 2009 excise tax increase in China has resulted in higher tax revenue for the government and lower profits for the tobacco industry, with no increase in the retail price of cigarettes for consumers.

Published government tobacco tax documentation and statistics published by the Chinese STMA (state tobacco monopoly administration) are used to analyse the interrelations among industry profits, taxes and retail price of cigarettes in China.
To explain China's cigarette pricing mechanism and the role of the Chinese State Tobacco Monopoly Administration (STMA (state tobacco monopoly administration)) on cigarette pricing and taxation.

Of study participants, 36% were male. Prevalence of casual high BP (blood pressure) was 19%. In the population, 10% were current cigarette smokers and habitual alcohol use was high at 56%. As measured by body mass index, 2% were obese and 14% had abdominal obesity. RHR (resting heart rate) was elevated (>90 bpm) in 19%. Individuals with an elevated RHR (resting heart rate) had a higher risk (OR 1.94, 95% CI (confidence interval) 1.15-3.26%, p = 0.013) of casual high BP (blood pressure) compared with participants with normal RHR (resting heart rate) independently of several established CVD (cardiovascular disease) risk factors. An index of smoking susceptibility was created using measures of cigarette use and future intention to smoke. A zero-order correlation for parental restriction of R-rated movie viewing and smoking susceptibility showed a strong association (r = -.36, p<.001). A hierarchical logistic regression yielded odds ratios (ORs (odds ratios)) for being susceptible to or having tried smoking for three levels of parental R-rated movie restriction. Results show that compared to full restriction, respondents with partial or no restriction were more likely to be susceptible to smoking (partial restriction: OR = 2.1, 95% CI (confidence interval) = 1.5-2.8; no restriction: OR = 3.3, 95% CI (confidence interval) = 2.3-4.6), when controlling for demographic factors, and family and friend smoking. Analyses using a measure of smoking prevalence as the dependent variable yielded similar results (partial restriction: OR = 1.5, 95% CI (confidence interval) = 1.0-2.2; no restriction: OR = 2.5, 95% CI (confidence interval) = 1.7-3.7).
results.reference: Numerous studies have found that taxation is one of the most effective policy instruments for tobacco control. However, these findings come from countries that have market economies where market forces determine prices and influence how cigarette taxes are passed to the consumers in retail prices. China's tobacco industry is not a market economy; therefore, non-market forces and the current Chinese tobacco monopoly system determine cigarette prices. The result is that tax increases do not necessarily get passed on to the retail price.

results.question: Vertical lines in distal esophageal mucosa (VLEM): a true endoscopic manifestation of esophagitis in children?

results.answer:
The presence of vertical lines in the esophageal mucosa (VLEM) was observed as the only mucosal abnormality in a group of children, and most of these children had eosinophilic esophagitis confirmed histologically. The low rate of normal histology in biopsies from patients with VLEM (2.4%) compared to those with normal mucosa (57.5%) supports VLEM as a true endoscopic manifestation of esophagitis in children.

yes
contexts: We observed an endoscopic abnormally in a group of children with histological esophagitis. We termed this finding "vertical lines in esophageal mucosa" (VLEM). We examined the relationship between the presence of VLEM and significant histologic changes in esophageal mucosal biopsies.
