Most patients in Group 2 had eosinophilic esophagitis (34 of 41, 83%, specificity 0.85, sensitivity 0.5, p>0.001) which was of moderate to severe intensity (31 of 34, 91.2%, specificity 0.88, sensitivity 0.73, p<0.001).

The procedure reports, available endoscopic photographs, and histology reports were reviewed to establish the endoscopic and histologic appearance of the esophageal mucosa. Intraepithelial cells were counted in a blind review of 42 randomly selected biopsies.
Five men underwent endoscopy because of dysphagia confirmed (clinically, endoscopically, and histologically) to be caused by primary eosinophilic esophagitis and were treated by bouginage.
results.reference: Histology usually demonstrated moderate to severe inflammation when VLEM were present. VLEM may be a highly specific endoscopic feature of esophagitis in children.

contexts: Ischemia-reperfusion (IR (ischemia-reperfusion)) injury remains a major cause of early morbidity and mortality after lung transplantation with poorly documented extrapulmonary repercussions. Fifty-seven consecutive patients were included. The average age was 64.4 ± 10.7, 73% of the patients were males, and nearly half of the patients were known to have ischemic heart disease. Fifty-four obese individuals (median body mass index (BMI (body mass index)) 43.0 kg/m(2)), 52 % of whom had OSA (apnoea-hypopnoea index (AHI) ≥ 15), had a median 95th centile autoCPAP pressure of 11.8 cmH2O. contexts: Traumatic aortic injury (TAI (traumatic aortic injury)) is a rare but life-threatening type of injury. We investigate whether the anatomy of the aortic arch influences the severity of aortic injury.

The mean aortic arch index and mean aortic arch angle were 6.8 cm and 58.3°, respectively, in the type I injury group; 4.4 cm and 45.9° in the type III group; 3.3 cm and 37° in the type IV group. This study was performed to evaluate the significance of the WBC (white blood cell count) count at presentation in the blunt trauma patients.
results.reference: The severity of TAI is influenced by the sharpness of the aortic arch. There is an inverse relationship between the severity of aortic injury and the aortic arch index.

However, it is less useful for predicting head, chest, or abdomen injuries individually, and its ability to predict mortality only approached statistical significance. Overall, the evidence supports that the classification predicts mortality, transfusion needs, and some non-orthopaedic injuries.

yes
contexts: The objectives of this study were to evaluate the ability of the Young-Burgess classification system to predict mortality, transfusion requirements, and nonorthopaedic injuries in patients with pelvic ring fractures and to determine whether mortality rates after pelvic fractures have changed over time.

The Young-Burgess system differentiated transfusion requirements--lateral compression Type 3 (LC3 (lateral compression type 3)) and anteroposterior compression Types 2 (APC2 (anteroposterior compression types 2)) and 3 (APC3 (apc2) and 3)) fractures had higher transfusion requirements than did lateral compression Type 1 (LC1 (lateral compression type 1)), anteroposterior compression Type 1 (APC1 (anteroposterior compression type 1)), and vertical shear (VS (vertical shear)) (P<0.05)--but was not as useful at predicting head, chest, or abdomen injuries. Dividing fractures into stable and unstable types allowed the system to predict mortality rates, abdomen injury rates, and transfusion requirements. Overall mortality in the study group was 9.1%, unchanged from original Young-Burgess studies 15 years previously (P = 0.3).

results.reference: The Young-Burgess system is useful for predicting transfusion requirements. results.question: Is unsafe sexual behaviour increasing among HIV-infected individuals?

results.answer:
The data from the Swiss HIV Cohort Study (abstracts [1], [2], and [4]) indicate no evidence of an increase in reported unsafe sexual behavior among HIV-infected individuals over time, with an odds ratio of 1.0 and a confidence interval that includes no change. There was no evidence of an increase in reported unsafe sex over time in this population [odds ratio (OR (odds ratio)), 1.0; 95% confidence interval (CI (confidence interval)), 0.96-1.05]. Females (OR (odds ratio), 1.38; 95% CI (confidence interval), 1.19-1.60), 15-30 year olds (OR (odds ratio), 1.26; 95% CI (confidence interval), 1.09-1.47), those with HIV (human immunodeficiency virus)-positive partners (OR (odds ratio), 12.58; 95% CI (confidence interval), 10.84-14.07) and those with occasional partners (OR (odds ratio), 3.25; 95% CI (confidence interval), 2.87-3.67) were more likely to report unsafe sex. There was no evidence of a response bias over time, but individuals were less willing to leave questions about their sexual behaviour unanswered or ambiguous (OR (odds ratio), 0.93; 95% CI (confidence interval), 0.90-0.97).

The annual AIDS (acquired immunodeficiency syndrome) incidence rate in Jamaica increased only marginally in the past three years from 18.5 per 100000 population to 21.4 in 1997. Among those at high risk, HIV (human immunodeficiency virus) prevalence rates have risen to 6.3% (95% confidence interval 5.0-8.0) in STD (sexually transmitted disease) clinic attenders, around 10% and 21% in female prostitutes in Kingston and Montego Bay respectively and approximately 30% among homosexuals. Syphilis rates and congenital syphilis cases have declined. The proportion of men aged 15-49 years reporting sex with a non-regular partner declined from 35% in 1994 to 26% in 1996 (P<0.001). Women ever having used condoms increased from 51% in 1988 to 62.5% in 1992 and 73% in 1994 and 1996 (P<0.001), while condom use with a non-regular partner increased from 37% in 1992 to 73% in 1996 (P= 0.006). Condom use among men was high over the period: around 81% had ever used condoms and 77% used them with non-regular partners. Gay men, inner-city adults and adolescents aged 12-14 years all reported increases in condom use while condom sales and distribution increased from around 2 million in 1985 to 10 million in 1995.

The number of new diagnoses of HIV (human immunodeficiency virus) infection is rising in the northwestern hemisphere and it is becoming increasingly important to understand the mechanisms behind this trend.

In the period ranging from 1997 to 2003, 62 patients with EA (esophageal atresia) underwent preoperative TBS (tracheobronchoscopy). results.question: Are financial incentives cost-effective to support smoking cessation during pregnancy?

results.answer:
The study indicates that financial incentives for smoking cessation in pregnancy have an incremental cost per quitter comparable to standard values and result in a gain in quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) with an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER) of £482/QALY, which is well below the typical willingness-to-pay threshold of £30,000/QALY. The life-time model resulted in an incremental cost of £17 [95% confidence interval (CI (confidence interval)) = -£93, £107] and a gain of 0.04 QALYs (95% CI (confidence interval) = -0.058, 0.145), giving an ICER of £482/QALY ($734/QALY). results.question: Can bone thickness and inter-radicular space affect miniscrew placement in posterior mandibular sites?

contexts: Measurement of basal metabolic rate (BMR (basal metabolic rate)) is suggested as a tool to estimate energy requirements. Subjects were 121 men and 111 women (age: 21-67 years, BMI (body mass index): 16-41 kg/m(2)). Height, weight, and BMR (basal metabolic rate) were measured. Secondary analyses of cross-sectional data from the WHO (World Health Organization) study on Global Ageing and Adult Health in China, Mexico, Russia and South Africa (2007-2010). results.reference: Our results suggest that depressed vessel compliance and increased vascular resistance are features of young, obese, normotensive subjects independently of and in addition to cardiovascular risk factors. A number of patients, however, discontinue the gluten-free diet (GFD (gluten-free diet)) without developing symptoms or signs. The aim of our study was to investigate whether CD (celiac disease) patients are capable of developing tolerance to gluten.

A retrospective study of prepubertal children aged 3-12 years with CD (n=24) who were compared to prepubertal, non-CD (celiac disease) children of the same age (n=50). Children were included in the study if they had a diagnosis of CD (celiac disease) by intestinal biopsy, and were not on a gluten-free diet (GFD (gluten-free diet)). Patients were excluded if they had diseases of calcium or vitamin D metabolism, or were receiving calcium or vitamin D supplementation or had other autoimmune diseases. All subjects had their serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25(OH)D] level measured.

Celiac disease (CD (celiac disease)) is an autoimmune enteropathy characterized by villus atrophy and malabsorption of essential nutrients. Vitamin D deficiency has been described in autoimmune diseases, but its status in prepubertal children with CD (celiac disease) has not been adequately studied.
results.reference: Development of tolerance to gluten seems possible in some patients with CD. Further follow-up will show whether this tolerance is permanent or only a long-term return to latency. This feature may be associated with genetic characteristics, especially with HLA genotypes that differ from DQ2 or DQ8. More insight into the mechanisms of the development of gluten tolerance may help to distinguish those CD patients that might not require life-long GFD.

results.question: Do symptoms predict COPD in smokers?
rewritten_queries: symptoms predictive value COPD smokers
clinical features COPD diagnosis smoking patients
results.answer:
The data show that 92% of smokers with airways obstruction (a marker for COPD) report respiratory symptoms, and the odds ratios for symptoms like cough, dyspnea, sputum, and wheeze are elevated in smokers with airways obstruction. This indicates that symptoms are strongly associated with COPD in smokers, supporting the idea that symptoms can predict COPD in this group.

yes
contexts: Report of symptoms, smoking history, and spirometric data were collected from subjects screened for a work-related medical evaluation (N = 3,955). Prevalence of airflow obstruction and respiratory symptoms were assessed. Sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative predictive values, and relative risks of predicting symptoms and smoking history for COPD (chronic obstructive pulmonary disease) were calculated.

Forty-four percent of smokers in our sample had airways obstruction (AO (airways obstruction)). Of these, 36% reported a diagnosis of or treatment for COPD (chronic obstructive pulmonary disease). Odds ratio (95% CI (confidence interval)) for AO (airways obstruction) with smoking (>or = 20 pack-years) was 3.73 (3.12- 4.45), 1.98 (1.73-2.27) for cough, 1.79 (1.55-2.08) for dyspnea, 1.95 (1.70-2.34) for sputum, and 2.59 (2.26-2.97) for wheeze. Respiratory symptoms were reported by 92% of smokers with AO (airways obstruction), 86% smokers with restriction, 76% smokers with normal spirometry, and 73% of nonsmokers. Sensitivity (92% vs 90%), specificity (19% vs 22%), positive (47% vs 40%) and negative (75% vs 80%) predictive values for the presence of one or more symptoms were similar between smokers and all subjects.

The US (ultrasound) Preventive Services Task Force recommends against spirometry in the absence of symptoms. However, as much as 50% of COPD (chronic obstructive pulmonary disease) cases in the United States remain undiagnosed.

An index of smoking susceptibility was created using measures of cigarette use and future intention to smoke. A zero-order correlation for parental restriction of R-rated movie viewing and smoking susceptibility showed a strong association (r = -.36, p<.001). A hierarchical logistic regression yielded odds ratios (ORs (odds ratios)) for being susceptible to or having tried smoking for three levels of parental R-rated movie restriction. Results show that compared to full restriction, respondents with partial or no restriction were more likely to be susceptible to smoking (partial restriction: OR = 2.1, 95% CI (confidence interval) = 1.5-2.8; no restriction: OR = 3.3, 95% CI (confidence interval) = 2.3-4.6), when controlling for demographic factors, and family and friend smoking. Analyses using a measure of smoking prevalence as the dependent variable yielded similar results (partial restriction: OR = 1.5, 95% CI (confidence interval) = 1.0-2.2; no restriction: OR = 2.5, 95% CI (confidence interval) = 1.7-3.7).

For COPD (chronic obstructive pulmonary disease) and a collection of acute conditions the reliability of a single physician review was quite low (intra-class correlation = 0.16-0.26) but comparable to most previously published estimates for the use of this method in inpatient settings. However, for diabetes and hypertension the reliability is significantly higher at 0.46. The higher reliability is a result of the reviewers collectively being able to distinguish more differences in the quality of care between patients (p<0.007) and not due to less random noise or individual reviewer bias in the measurement. For these conditions the level of true quality (i.e. the rating of quality of care that would result from the full population of physician reviewers reviewing a record) varied from poor to good across patients.
results.reference: COPD is underdiagnosed in the United States. Symptoms are frequent in subjects with AO and increase their risk for COPD, but add little beyond age and smoking history to the predictive value of spirometry. In view of the high prevalence of symptoms and their poor predictive value, a simpler and more effective approach would be to screen older smokers.

results.question: Search engine as a diagnostic tool in difficult immunological and allergologic cases: is Google useful?
rewritten_queries: Search engine diagnostic tool immunology allergy cases
effectiveness Google medical diagnosis immunology allergy
use of internet search engines in complex immunological diagnosis
results.answer:
The study described in the abstracts evaluated the effectiveness of Google searches in diagnosing complex immunological and allergic cases. The results showed that investigators using Google were able to provide correct diagnoses in a majority of cases (64%-86%), indicating that Google can be a useful diagnostic tool in these difficult cases. Therefore, the evidence supports the usefulness of Google in this context.

yes
contexts: Web search engines are an important tool in communication and diffusion of knowledge. Among these, Google appears to be the most popular one: in August 2008, it accounted for 87% of all web searches in the UK, compared with Yahoo's 3.3%. Google's value as a diagnostic guide in general medicine was recently reported. The aim of this comparative cross-sectional study was to evaluate whether searching Google with disease-related terms was effective in the identification and diagnosis of complex immunological and allergic cases.

Forty-five case reports were randomly selected by an independent observer from peer-reviewed medical journals. Clinical data were presented separately to three investigators, blinded to the final diagnoses. Investigator A was a Consultant with an expert knowledge in Internal Medicine and Allergy (IM&A) and basic computing skills. Investigator B was a Registrar in IM&A. Investigator C was a Research Nurse. Both Investigators B and C were familiar with computers and search engines. For every clinical case presented, each investigator independently carried out an Internet search using Google to provide a final diagnosis. Their results were then compared with the published diagnoses.
To determine the diagnostic usefulness of cytokeratin 7/20 immunostaining for short-segment Barrett's oesophagus in Korea.

Correct diagnoses were provided in 30/45 (66%) cases, 39/45 (86%) cases, and in 29/45 (64%) cases by investigator A, B, and C, respectively. All of the three investigators achieved the correct diagnosis in 19 cases (42%), and all of them failed in two cases.

The identification of the most suspect enhancing part of a lesion is regarded as a major diagnostic criterion in dynamic magnetic resonance mammography. Computer-aided diagnosis (CAD (computer-aided diagnosis)) software allows the semi-automatic analysis of the kinetic characteristics of complete enhancing lesions, providing additional information about lesion vasculature. The diagnostic value of this information has not yet been quantified.
results.reference: This Google-based search was useful to identify an appropriate diagnosis in complex immunological and allergic cases. Computing skills may help to get better results.

results.question: Uniformity of evidence-based treatments in practice?
rewritten_queries: adherence evidence-based medicine clinical practice variability
implementation evidence-based guidelines healthcare settings
barriers uniform application evidence-based treatments
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate variability in the implementation of evidence-based treatments (EBTs) in clinical practice. Abstract [1] highlights that measurement-based care, an evidence-based approach, is not commonly used in routine depression treatment, suggesting inconsistency. Abstract [2] discusses variability in outcomes based on therapist characteristics, implying non-uniform application. Therefore, evidence-based treatments are not uniformly applied in practice.

no
contexts: The gap between evidence-based treatments and routine care has been well established. Findings from the Sequenced Treatments Alternatives to Relieve Depression (STAR*D) emphasized the importance of measurement-based care for the treatment of depression as a key ingredient for achieving response and remission; yet measurement-based care approaches are not commonly used in clinical practice.

Various factors contribute to the effective implementation of evidence-based treatments (EBTs (evidence-based treatments)). In this study, cognitive processing therapy (CPT (cognitive processing therapy)) was administered in a Veterans Affairs (VA (veterans affairs)) posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD (posttraumatic stress disorder)) specialty clinic in which training and supervision were provided following VA (veterans affairs) implementation guidelines. The aim was to (a) estimate the proportion of variability in outcome attributable to therapists and (b) identify characteristics of those therapists who produced better outcomes.

Articles were assessed according to the criteria of the Evidence-Based Medicine Working Group for evaluating articles on harm. Review of the literature yielded estimates of the risk of adverse fertility outcomes ranging from 1.6 (95% confidence interval [CI (confidence interval)] 1.1 to 2.5) for ectopic pregnancy after an appendectomy to 4.8 (95% CI (confidence interval) 1.5 to 14.9) for tubal infertility from perforation of the appendix. Recall bias, and poor adjustment for confounding variables in some reports, weakened the validity of the studies.

Adoption and implementation of evidence-based measures for catheter care leads to reductions in central line-associated bloodstream infection (CLABSI (central line-associated bloodstream infection)) rates in the NICU (neonatal intensive care unit). The purpose of this study is to evaluate whether this rate reduction is sustainable for at least 1 year and to identify key determinants of this sustainability at the NICU (neonatal intensive care unit) of the Floating Hospital for Children at Tufts Medical Center.

We sought to develop a more reliable structured implicit chart review instrument for use in assessing the quality of care for chronic disease and to examine if ratings are more reliable for conditions in which the evidence base for practice is more developed.
results.reference: This study adds to the growing body of literature documenting the importance of the individual therapist as an important factor in the change process.

results.question: Do approved doctors and medical referees in the UK agree when assessing a seafarer's fitness?
rewritten_queries: approved doctors medical referees agreement seafarer fitness assessment UK
seafarer medical fitness evaluation UK guidelines
discrepancies between doctors and medical referees seafarer fitness UK
results.answer:
The evidence shows that the overall agreement between Approved Doctors and Medical Referees when assessing a seafarer's fitness is poor, with a Kappa value of 0.18 indicating low concordance. Additionally, there are significant differences in how each group classifies fitness categories, with Medical Referees often assigning less severe fitness restrictions than Approved Doctors. Therefore, they do not agree well in their assessments.

no
contexts: The seafaring industry remains a hazardous occupation that requires sophisticated systems of risk and fitness assessment. This study aims to investigate the extent of agreement between Approved Doctors (ADs (approved doctors)) and Medical Referees (MRs (medical referees)) when they assess a seafarer's fitness.

Between 2003 and 2009 a total of 232,878 seafarer medical examinations were carried out by ADs (approved doctors), of which 465 were considered by the MRs (medical referees) because the seafarer appealed against the AD (Alzheimer disease)'s decision. The extent of agreement between ADs (approved doctors) and MRs (medical referees) was studied.

Two hundred and sixty-eight (58%) cases seen by the ADs (approved doctors) were classed as category 4 "permanently unfit"; the referees only placed 85 (18%) of them in this category. On the other hand, 252 (54%) cases seen by the MRs (medical referees) were classed as category 2 "fit with restrictions", while the ADs (approved doctors) had only placed 111 (24%) in this category. The overall agreement between the assessors (AD (Alzheimer disease) vs. MR) was poor (Kappa K = 0.18).

For cardiovascular diseases and for mental ill-health, access to additional information by the MR was the commonest reason for changing the fitness category, but for all other conditions factors such as the experience and knowledge of the MRs (medical referees) or their different interpretation of the standards were the most frequent reasons for a change to fitness category or to restrictions.
A hospital orthodontic department (Chesterfield Royal Hospital, UK).
results.reference: This study found that there was poor agreement between the AD's decision and the subsequent MR's decision regarding the fitness of those seafarers who decided to appeal against the AD's initial assessment. The reasons for this are considered.

results.question: Hepatorenal syndrome: are we missing some prognostic factors?
rewritten_queries: hepatorenal syndrome prognostic factors
hepatorenal syndrome mortality predictors
hepatorenal syndrome risk stratification recent studies
results.answer:
The provided abstracts identify several prognostic factors for survival in hepatorenal syndrome, such as serum creatinine, urinary sodium, gender, performance status, pain, and dysphagia. However, treatment modalities, dialysis use, and age were not associated with survival, and the introduction notes that ascites volume and anthropometric assessments are not routinely documented or considered in prognostic evaluation, suggesting potential missing factors. Therefore, the evidence supports that some prognostic factors may still be missing.

yes
contexts: Hepatorenal syndrome (HRS (hepatorenal syndrome)) is the functional renal failure associated with advanced cirrhosis and has also been described in fulminant hepatic failure. Without liver transplantation its prognosis is dismal. Our study included patients with type 1 HRS (hepatorenal syndrome) associated with cirrhosis, who were not liver transplant candidates.AIM: To identify variables associated with improved survival.

Median survival was 13 days for the whole group. Survival varied with the end-stage liver disease (ESLD (end-stage liver disease)) etiology: autoimmune, 49 days, cardiac cirrhosis, 22 days, idiopathic, 15.5 days, viral, 15 days, hepatitis C and alcohol, 14.5 days, alcohol 8 days, and neoplasia 4 days (p = 0.048). Survival of HRS (hepatorenal syndrome) associated with alcoholic liver disease versus other etiologies was not statistically significant (p = 0.1). Increased serum creatinine (p = 0.02) and urinary sodium 6-10 mEq/l (p = 0.027) at the initiation of therapy were prognostic factors for mortality. HRS (hepatorenal syndrome) treatment modalities (p = 0.73), use of dialysis (p = 0.56), dialysis modality (p = 0.35), use of vasopressors (p = 0.26), pre-existing renal disease (p = 0.49), gender (p = 0.90), and age (p = 0.57) were not associated with survival.

Sixty-eight patients fulfilled the revised Ascites Club Criteria for type 1 HRS (hepatorenal syndrome). None of them was suitable for liver transplantation. All the patients were treated with combinations of: albumin, midodrine and octreotide, pressors, and hemodialysis.

The final multivariate Cox regression model retained four parameters as independent prognostic factors for survival: male gender with a hazard ratio (HR (hazard ratio)) = 1.32 (95% CI (confidence interval) 1.03-1.69; P = 0.03); performance status (0 to 1 versus 2) with HR (hazard ratio) = 1.63 (95% CI (confidence interval) 1.04-2.54; P = 0.032); patient's self-reported score of pain with HR (hazard ratio)= 1.11 (95% CI (confidence interval) 1.07-1.16; P<0.001) and dysphagia with HR (hazard ratio) = 1.12 (95% CI (confidence interval) 1.04-1.21; P = 0.003). A 10-point shift worse in the scale measuring pain and dysphagia translated into an 11% and 12% increased in the likelihood of death respectively. A risk group categorization was also developed.

Ascitis and undernutrition are frequent complications of cirrhosis, however ascitis volume and anthropometric assessment are not routinely documented or considered in prognostic evaluation. In a homogeneous cohort followed during two years these variables were scrutinized, aiming to ascertain relevance for longterm outcome.
results.reference: We report for the first time ESLD etiology as a prognostic factor for survival. The renal function (expressed as serum creatinine) and urinary Na (<5 mEq/l) at the time of diagnosis were found to be associated with survival, suggesting that early treatment might increase survival.

results.question: Vaginal dose assessment in image-guided brachytherapy for cervical cancer: Can we really rely on dose-point evaluation?
rewritten_queries: vaginal dose assessment image-guided brachytherapy cervical cancer
reliability dose-point evaluation brachytherapy cervical cancer
dosimetry methods vaginal dose brachytherapy cervical cancer
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that dose-point evaluation at PIBS points in image-guided brachytherapy shows strong correlation between prescribed and delivered doses, with insignificant applicator movement affecting dose delivery. Although some dose variations were noted at other points (e.g., rectovaginal point), the overall data support the reliability of dose-point evaluation for vaginal dose assessment.

yes
contexts: Although dose-volume parameters in image-guided brachytherapy have become a standard, the use of posterior-inferior border of the pubic symphysis (PIBS (posterior-inferior border of the pubic symphysis)) points has been recently proposed in the reporting of vaginal doses. The aim was to evaluate their pertinence.

Nineteen patients who received image-guided brachytherapy after concurrent radiochemotherapy were included. Per treatment, CT scans were performed at Days 2 and 3, with reporting of the initial dwell positions and times. Doses delivered to the PIBS (posterior-inferior border of the pubic symphysis) points were evaluated on each plan, considering that they were representative of one-third of the treatment. The movements of the applicator according to the PIBS (posterior-inferior border of the pubic symphysis) point were analysed.

Compared with computed tomography (CT (computed tomography)) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI (magnetic resonance imaging)), positron emission tomography (PET (positron emission tomography)) may have additional value in the assessment of primary and recurrent cervical cancer. However, the degree of tumour uptake of (18)F-2-fluoro-2-deoxy-D: -glucose (FDG (fluoro-2-deoxy-d: -glucose)) uptake is sometimes influenced by diabetes mellitus (DM (diabetes mellitus)). Therefore, we conducted this prospective study to compare the diagnostic ability of FDG (fluoro-2-deoxy-d: -glucose)-PET (positron emission tomography) in patients with cervical cancer complicated by DM (diabetes mellitus) and those without DM (diabetes mellitus).

A retrospective analysis of 136 breasts of 134 patients, who received breast-conserving oncoplastic surgery for low-risk breast cancer between 2002 and 2010 in the Universities of Vienna and Luebeck followed by adjuvant APBI (accelerated partial breast irradiation) applying total doses of pulse dose rate of 50.4 Gy or high-dose rate (HDR (high-dose rate)) of 32 Gy over 4 days. Target volume definition was performed by the use of surgical-free margin data, related to intraoperatively fixed clip positions, pre- and postoperative imaging, and palpation.

Mean prescribed doses at PIBS (posterior-inferior border of the pubic symphysis) -2, PIBS (posterior-inferior border of the pubic symphysis), PIBS (posterior-inferior border of the pubic symphysis) +2 were, respectively, 2.23 ± 1.4, 6.39 ± 6.6, and 31.85 ± 36.06 Gy. Significant differences were observed between the 5 patients with vaginal involvement and the remaining 14 at the level of PIBS (posterior-inferior border of the pubic symphysis) +2 and PIBS (posterior-inferior border of the pubic symphysis): +47.60 Gy and +7.46 Gy, respectively (p = 0.023 and 0.03). The variations between delivered and prescribed doses at PIBS (posterior-inferior border of the pubic symphysis) points were not significant. However, at International commission on radiation units and measurements rectovaginal point, the delivered dose was decreased by 1.43 ± 2.49 Gy from the planned dose (p = 0.019). The delivered doses at the four points were strongly correlated with the prescribed doses with R(2) ranging from 0.93 to 0.95. The movements of the applicator in regard of the PIBS (posterior-inferior border of the pubic symphysis) point assessed with the Digital Imaging and Communications in Medicine coordinates were insignificant.
results.reference: The doses evaluated at PIBS points are not impacted by intrafractional movements. PIBS and PIBS +2 dose points allow distinguishing the plans of patients with vaginal infiltration. Further studies are needed to correlate these parameters with vaginal morbidity.

results.question: Prescriptions as a proxy for asthma in children: a good choice?
rewritten_queries: asthma diagnosis children prescription validity
use of prescriptions as proxy for asthma epidemiology pediatric
accuracy prescriptions asthma identification children
results.answer:
The abstract by Stock et al. (reference [2]) discusses the use of prescription data to estimate asthma prevalence in children and highlights the need to critically assess and discuss various aspects of this approach. Additionally, reference [5] replicates Stock et al.'s method and compares prevalence estimates using prescription data with health survey data, implying that prescription data can be used but may require careful interpretation. This suggests that prescriptions can serve as a proxy for asthma in children, but with some limitations.

yes
contexts: A Medline search was conducted on the use of dexamethasone in the treatment of asthma exacerbations in children. The studies selected were clinical trials comparing the efficacy of dexamethasone with prednisone. Meta-analysis was performed examining physician revisitation rates and symptomatic return to baseline.

Stock et al. (Eur Respir J 25:47-53, 2005) recently estimated asthma prevalence in Germany using claims data on prescriptions and hospital diagnoses and found high prevalence peaks in infants. Our objective was to critically assess and discuss various aspects of identifying children with asthma using prescription data.

A short course of systemic corticosteroids is an important therapy in the treatment of pediatric asthma exacerbations. Although a 5-day course of oral prednisone or prednisolone has become the most commonly used regimen, dexamethasone has also been used for a shorter duration (1-2 days) with potential for improvement in compliance and palatability. We reviewed the literature to determine if there is sufficient evidence that dexamethasone can be used as an effective alternative in the treatment of pediatric asthma exacerbations in the inpatient setting.

To characterize the use and delivery of cough and cold medicines in children younger than 6 presenting to an inner-city pediatric emergency department (PED (pediatric emergency department)) following 2007 FDA (Food and Drug Administration) warnings.

We replicated the selection procedure of Stock et al. using data on 290,919 children aged 0-17 years insured in the Gmünder ErsatzKasse (GEK (gmünder ersatzkasse)) in 2005. Asthma prevalence was also estimated in a sample of 17,641 children aged 0-17 years participating in the German Health Interview and Examination Survey for Children and Adolescents (KiGGS) from 2003 to 2006.
results.reference: When additional validation studies were taken into account, asthma medications were found to be prescribed not only for asthma but also for other respiratory diseases. In addition, not all children with current asthma had prescriptions. We therefore conclude that asthma medications are therefore not a good proxy for the disease.

results.question: Does the familial transmission of drinking patterns persist into young adulthood?
rewritten_queries: familial transmission alcohol drinking patterns young adulthood
intergenerational alcohol use behavior persistence young adults
results.answer:
The study found that young adults from abstaining families drank less than those from non-abstaining families, but the differences across drinking levels were not statistically significant, and actual drinking levels in drinking families were weakly or not associated with offspring drinking. This suggests that while there is some indication of familial influence, the transmission of drinking patterns into young adulthood is not strongly supported.

no
contexts: To explore the long-term (10-year) transmission of familial drinking during adolescence to offspring drinking patterns in young adulthood.

Swedish longitudinal study, assessing the relationship between familial drinking in 2000 and offspring drinking in 2010 using simultaneous quantile regression analysis (n=744).DATA: Data on familial drinking was gathered from the Swedish level-of-living surveys (LNU (living surveys)) and from partner LNU (living surveys) in 2000 while data on offspring drinking in young adulthood was gathered from LNU (living surveys) 2010. Drinking among offspring, parents and potential stepparents was measured through identical quantity-frequency indices referring to the past 12 months in 2010 and 2000 respectively.

Young adults whose families were abstainers in 2000 drank substantially less across quintiles in 2010 than offspring of non-abstaining families. The difference, however, was not statistically significant between quintiles of the conditional distribution. Actual drinking levels in drinking families were not at all or weakly associated with drinking in offspring. Supplementary analyses confirmed these patterns.

Parental drinking has been shown to be associated with offspring drinking. However, the relationship appears to be more complex than often assumed and few studies have tracked it over longer time periods.
To explore the extent to which parent-adolescent emotional closeness, family conflict, and parental permissiveness moderate the association of puberty and alcohol use in adolescents (aged 10-14).
results.reference: The association between familial drinking and offspring drinking in young adulthood exhibits clear non-linear trends. Changes in the lower part of the familial drinking distribution are strongly related to drinking in young adults, but the actual levels of drinking in drinking families appear less important in shaping the drinking patterns of the offspring in young adulthood.

results.question: Proof of concept study: does fenofibrate have a role in sleep apnoea syndrome?
rewritten_queries: fenofibrate sleep apnoea syndrome
fenofibrate effect on sleep apnea
fenofibrate respiratory function sleep apnea
results.answer:
The study showed that fenofibrate significantly reduced the percentage of time with low oxygen saturation and decreased obstructive apnoeas and non-cortical micro-awakenings in patients with sleep apnoea syndrome. Although there was no significant change in the overall apnoea/hypopnoea index, these improvements suggest fenofibrate may have a beneficial role in sleep apnoea. 

yes
contexts: Proof-of-concept study comprising a placebo run-in period (1 week, 5 weeks if fibrate washout was required) and a 4-week randomized, double-blind treatment period. Thirty-four subjects (mean age 55 years, body mass index 34 kg/m 2 , fasting triglycerides 3.5 mmol/L) with diagnosed sleep apnoea syndrome not treated with continuous positive airways pressure were enrolled and randomized to once daily treatment with fenofibrate (145 mg NanoCrystal(R) tablet) or placebo. Overnight polysomnography, computerized attention/vigilance tests and blood sampling for measurement of lipids, insulin, fasting plasma glucose and fibrinogen were performed at the end of each study period.
To investigate the effect of fenofibrate on sleep apnoea indices.

Fenofibrate treatment significantly reduced the percentage of time with SpO(2)<90% (from 9.0% to 3.5% vs. 10.0% to 11.5% with placebo, p = 0.007), although there was no significant change in the AHI (reduction vs. control 14% (95%CI (confidence interval) -47 to 40%, p = 0.533). Treatment reduced obstructive apnoeas (by 44%, from 18.5 at baseline to 15.0 at end of treatment vs. 29.0 to 30.5 on placebo, p = 0.048), and non-cortical micro-awakenings per hour (from 23.5 to 18.0 vs. 24.0 to 25.0 with placebo, p = 0.004). Other sleep variables were not significantly influenced by fenofibrate.
Exploratory study in patients with mild to moderate sleep apnoea, limited treatment duration; concomitant hypnotic treatment (35%); lack of correction for multiplicity of testing.

As this was an exploratory study, a range of sleep variables were evaluated. The apnoea/hypopnoea index (AHI (apnoea/hypopnoea index)) and percentage of time spent with arterial oxygen saturation (SpO(2))<90% were relevant as they have been evaluated in other clinical trials. Other variables included total apnoeas, hypopnoeas and oxygen desaturations, and non-cortical micro-awakenings related to respiratory events per hour.
results.reference: The consistent direction of change in sleep indices in this proof-of-concept study may support further investigation of fenofibrate in moderate to severe sleep apnoea syndrome.

results.question: Can mental imagery functional magnetic resonance imaging predict recovery in patients with disorders of consciousness?
rewritten_queries: mental imagery fMRI prediction recovery disorders of consciousness
functional MRI biomarkers prognosis disorders of consciousness patients
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that mental imagery fMRI can identify activation in specific brain regions in patients with disorders of consciousness, and this activation correlates with recovery outcomes. Specifically, all vegetative state patients showing activation improved to at least a minimally conscious state, demonstrating high sensitivity and specificity for predicting recovery. Therefore, mental imagery fMRI shows prognostic value in predicting recovery in these patients.

yes
contexts: To determine the potential prognostic value of using functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI (functional magnetic resonance imaging)) to identify patients with disorders of consciousness, who show potential for recovery.

Participants performed a mental imagery fMRI (functional magnetic resonance imaging) paradigm. They were asked to alternately imagine playing tennis and navigating through their home. In 14 of the 22 examined patients (VS, n=5; MCS, n=9), a significant activation of the regions of interest (ROIs (regions of interest)) of the mental imagery paradigm could be found. All 5 patients with activation of a significant blood oxygen level dependent signal, who were in a VS at the time of the fMRI (functional magnetic resonance imaging) examination, reached at least an MCS at the end of the observation period. In contrast, 5 participants in a VS who failed to show activation in ROIs (regions of interest), did not (sensitivity 100%, specificity 100%). Six of 9 patients in an MCS with activation in ROIs (regions of interest) emerged from an MCS. Of 3 patients in an MCS who did not show activation, 2 patients stayed in an MCS and 1 patient emerged from the MCS (sensitivity 85%, specificity 40%).

Disorders of consciousness (DOC (disorders of consciousness)) diagnosis relies on the presence or absence of purposeful motor responsiveness, which characterizes the minimally conscious state (MCS (minimally conscious state)) and the unresponsive wakefulness syndrome (UWS (unresponsive wakefulness syndrome)), respectively. Functional neuroimaging studies have raised the question of possible residual conscious awareness also in clinically-defined UWS (unresponsive wakefulness syndrome) patients. The aim of our study was to identify electrophysiological parameters, by means of a transcranial magnetic stimulation approach, which might potentially express the presence of residual networks sustaining fragmentary behavioral patterns, even when no conscious behavior can be observed.
To investigate the importance of loss of consciousness (LOC (loss of consciousness)) in predicting neuropsychological test performance in a large sample of patients with head injury.
Retrospective comparison of neuropsychological test results for patients who suffered traumatic LOC (loss of consciousness), no LOC (loss of consciousness), or uncertain LOC (loss of consciousness).
results.reference: The fMRI paradigm mental imagery displays a high concordance with the further clinical course of patients in a VS. All 5 patients in a VS who showed significant activation of ROIs had a favorable further course until the end of the observation period. We therefore propose the term "functional minimally conscious state" for these patients. They may benefit from rehabilitation treatment. In cases where no significant activation was seen, the method has no prognostic value. Prediction of the clinical course of patients in an MCS by fMRI was considerably less accurate than in patients in a VS.

results.question: The nurse cystoscopist: a feasible option?
rewritten_queries: nurse cystoscopist role feasibility
nurse-led cystoscopy outcomes
nurse practitioner cystoscopy scope practice
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that a trained urology nurse practitioner (UNP) and a consultant urologist showed very close agreement in detecting bladder tumors during flexible cystoscopy, with a Kappa value of 0.94. Only one tumor was missed by each examiner, both of which were minute, suggesting that the nurse cystoscopist is a feasible option for this procedure.

yes
contexts: Eighty-three patients underwent flexible cystoscopy by both the UNP (urology nurse practitioner) and consultant urologist, each unaware of the other's findings. Before comparing the findings, each declared whether there was tumour or any suspicious lesion requiring biopsy.

Of 83 patients examined by flexible cystoscopy, 26 were found to have a tumour or a suspicious lesion. One tumour was missed by the UNP (urology nurse practitioner) and one by the urologist; each tumour was minute. Analysis using the chance-corrected proportional agreement (Kappa) was 0.94, indicating very close agreement.
To compare the accuracy achieved by a trained urology nurse practitioner (UNP (urology nurse practitioner)) and consultant urologist in detecting bladder tumours during flexible cystoscopy.

We have previously reported the feasibility of diagnostic and therapeutic peritoneoscopy including liver biopsy, gastrojejunostomy, and tubal ligation by an oral transgastric approach. We present results of per-oral transgastric splenectomy in a porcine model. Among all single elderly individuals, 30 percent have mobility limitations, and an increase of $100 per month in the maximum SSI (supplemental security income) benefit caused the rate of mobility limitations to fall by 0.46 percentage points. The findings were robust to sensitivity analyses. First, analyses limited to those most likely to receive SSI (supplemental security income) produced larger effects, but analyses limited to those least likely to receive SSI (supplemental security income) produced no measurable effect. Second, varying the disability measure did not meaningfully alter the findings. Third, excluding the institutionalized, immigrants, individuals living in states with exceptionally large benefit changes, and individuals living in states with no SSI (supplemental security income) supplements did not change the substantive conclusions. Fourth, Medicaid did not confound the effects. Finally, these results were robust for married individuals.

The robust relationship between socioeconomic factors and health suggests that social and economic policies might substantially affect health, while other evidence suggests that medical care, the main focus of current health policy, may not be the primary determinant of population health. Income support policies are one promising avenue to improve population health. This study examines whether the federal cash transfer program to poor elderly, the Supplemental Security Income (SSI (supplemental security income)) program, affects old-age disability.

This study uses the 1990 and 2000 censuses, employing state and year fixed-effect models, to test whether within-state changes in maximum SSI (supplemental security income) benefits over time lead to changes in disability among people aged sixty-five and older.

An estimated 25.8 million adults aged 40-65 (26.7%) said they would be interested in paying for a public insurance program to cover PAS (personal assistance services) benefits. However, interest in PAS (personal assistance services) insurance varied by age, race, ethnicity, region, income, disability status, and family experience with ADL assistance. Only 1.6 million adults aged 40-65 (1.8%) said they would be willing to pay $100 per month or more for coverage.

To estimate the number of middle-aged adults interested in purchasing PAS (personal assistance services) insurance, the sociodemographic, socioeconomic and disability attributes of this population, and the maximum monthly premium they would be willing to pay for such coverage.
results.reference: Income support policy may be a significant new lever for improving population health, especially that of lower-income persons. Even though the findings are robust, further analyses are needed to confirm their reliability. Future research should examine a variety of different income support policies, as well as whether a broader range of social and economic policies affect health.

results.question: Profiling quality of care: Is there a role for peer review?
rewritten_queries: peer review quality of care healthcare
peer review impact clinical outcomes
peer review healthcare quality improvement
results.answer:
The provided abstracts describe the use of structured implicit peer review by physicians to assess the quality of care, showing that reliability varies by condition but can be significant, especially for diseases with a well-developed evidence base like diabetes and hypertension. This suggests that peer review has a role in profiling quality of care, as it can distinguish differences in care quality across patients. Therefore, the evidence supports the role of peer review in profiling quality of care.

yes
contexts: We conducted a reliability study in a cohort with patient records including both outpatient and inpatient care as the objects of measurement. We developed a structured implicit review instrument to assess the quality of care over one year of treatment. 12 reviewers conducted a total of 496 reviews of 70 patient records selected from 26 VA clinical sites in two regions of the country. Each patient had between one and four conditions specified as having a highly developed evidence base (diabetes and hypertension) or a less developed evidence base (chronic obstructive pulmonary disease or a collection of acute conditions). Multilevel analysis that accounts for the nested and cross-classified structure of the data was used to estimate the signal and noise components of the measurement of quality and the reliability of implicit review.

We sought to develop a more reliable structured implicit chart review instrument for use in assessing the quality of care for chronic disease and to examine if ratings are more reliable for conditions in which the evidence base for practice is more developed.

For COPD (chronic obstructive pulmonary disease) and a collection of acute conditions the reliability of a single physician review was quite low (intra-class correlation = 0.16-0.26) but comparable to most previously published estimates for the use of this method in inpatient settings. However, for diabetes and hypertension the reliability is significantly higher at 0.46. The higher reliability is a result of the reviewers collectively being able to distinguish more differences in the quality of care between patients (p<0.007) and not due to less random noise or individual reviewer bias in the measurement. For these conditions the level of true quality (i.e. the rating of quality of care that would result from the full population of physician reviewers reviewing a record) varied from poor to good across patients.

This study examines whether having a regular clinician for preventive care is associated with quality of care for young children, as measured by interpersonal quality ratings and content of anticipatory guidance.
A descriptive and clinical study, with review of patient data.
results.reference: For conditions with a well-developed quality of care evidence base, such as hypertension and diabetes, a single structured implicit review to assess the quality of care over a period of time is moderately reliable. This method could be a reasonable complement or alternative to explicit indicator approaches for assessing and comparing quality of care. Structured implicit review, like explicit quality measures, must be used more cautiously for illnesses for which the evidence base is less well developed, such as COPD and acute, short-course illnesses.

results.question: Eyelid-parotid metastasis: do we screen for coexisting masses?

eyelid tumor parotid gland metastasis diagnostic approach
management parotid metastasis from eyelid carcinoma
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that primary eyelid tumors can metastasize to the parotid gland and vice versa, and that histology and immunocytochemistry are used to differentiate primary tumors from metastases. This suggests that when one tumor is identified, screening for coexisting masses in the other site is clinically relevant to detect metastasis. Therefore, screening for coexisting masses in eyelid and parotid regions is supported.

yes
contexts: To report three cases illustrating that it is not unusual for a primary eyelid tumour to metastasise to the parotid gland and vice versa.

Two patients with malignant parotid tumours underwent radical parotidectomy and presented subsequently with eyelid lesions. Biopsy showed that both eyelid lesions were histologically similar to the primary parotid tumour. A third patient was noted to have ipsilateral upper eyelid and parotid gland tumours. Histology and immunocytochemistry were used to differentiate the primary tumour and the metastasis.

One hundred forty-nine consecutive patients with suspected tumors of the parotid gland were examined with an epiDWI sequence by using a 1.5T unit. Image analysis was performed by 2 radiologists independently, and the intraclass correlation coefficient was computed. Histologic diagnosis was obtained in every patient. For comparison of apparent diffusion coefficients (ADCs (apparent diffusion coefficients)), a paired 2-tailed Student t test with a Bonferroni correction was used.
Our aim was to determine the value of echo-planar diffusion-weighted MR imaging (epiDWI) in differentiating various types of primary parotid gland tumors.

We analyzed groups of 167 and 140 patients who were diagnosed with lymph node metastasis in the matched primary surgery group and NACT (neoadjuvant chemotherapy) group, respectively, and no significant difference was observed (p = 0.081). The incidence of lymph node metastasis was significantly decreased in the NACT (neoadjuvant chemotherapy)-responsive group compared to the non-responsive group (18.4% vs. 38.6%, P<0.001). The metastatic rates for every lymph node group also declined in the NACT (neoadjuvant chemotherapy)-responsive group except for the deep inguinal and the para-aortic lymph node groups. Clinical response, deep stromal, parametrial and lymph vascular invasions were independent risk factors for lymph node metastasis in the NACT (neoadjuvant chemotherapy) group. Furthermore, deep stromal invasion and lymph vascular invasion, but not the response to NACT (neoadjuvant chemotherapy), were independently associated with upper LNM. The number of lymph nodes involved, response to NACT (neoadjuvant chemotherapy), tumor histology and a positive vaginal margin were independent prognostic factors affecting DFS or OS rates in node-positive patients treated with NACT (neoadjuvant chemotherapy) plus radical surgery.
results.reference: These cases illustrate that tumours involving eyelids and parotid glands can present simultaneously or sequentially, and either of these structures could be the focus of primary or metastatic tumour. The important message for oculoplastic and parotid surgeons is to routinely assess both the periocular and parotid area when patients present with a mass in either structure.

results.question: Will CT ordering practices change if we educate residents about the potential effects of radiation exposure?

results.answer:
The study described in abstracts [1]-[3] shows that after educating residents about radiation exposure from CT scans, the number of CT scans ordered remained constant for 90% of residents and decreased for only 10%. However, some residents increased the use of alternative imaging modalities like MRI and ultrasound. This suggests that while education may not significantly reduce the overall number of CT orders, it can influence the choice of imaging techniques.

no
contexts: The aim of this study was to determine if educating residents about the potential effects of radiation exposure from computed tomographic (CT (computed tomographic)) imaging alters ordering patterns. This study also explored whether referring physicians are interested in radiation education and was an initial effort to address their CT (computed tomographic) ordering behavior.

Two to four months after a radiologist's lecture on the potential effects of radiation exposure related to CT (computed tomographic) scans, urology and orthopedic residents were surveyed regarding the number and types of CT (computed tomographic) scans they ordered, the use of alternative imaging modalities, and whether they used the lecture information to educate patients.

Twenty-one resident lecture attendants completed the survey. The number of CT (computed tomographic) scans ordered after the lecture stayed constant for 90% (19 of 21) and decreased for 10% (two of 21). The types of CT (computed tomographic) scans ordered changed after the lecture for 14% (three of 21). Thirty-three percent (seven of 21) reported increases in alternative imaging after the lecture, including 24% (five of 21) reporting increases in magnetic resonance imaging and 19% (four of 21) reporting increases in ultrasound. Patients directed questions about radiation exposure to 57% (12 of 21); 38% (eight of 21) used the lecture information to educate patients. Referring physicians were interested in the topic, and afterward, other physician groups requested radiation education lectures.

Digital tomosynthesis (DT (digital tomosynthesis)) is a new X-ray-based imaging technique that allows image enhancement with minimal increase in radiation exposure. The purpose of this study was to compare DT (digital tomosynthesis) with noncontrast computed tomography (NCCT (noncontrast computed tomography)) and to evaluate its potential role for the follow-up of patients with nephrolithiasis in a nonemergent setting.

We conducted a cross-sectional study at 9 academic medical centers. A questionnaire on US (ultrasound) education and bedside US (ultrasound) use was pilot tested and given to EM (emergency medicine) residents. The primary outcomes included the number of US (ultrasound) examinations performed, scope of bedside US (ultrasound) applications, barriers to residents' US (ultrasound) education, and US (ultrasound) use in the emergency department. The secondary outcomes were factors that would impact residents' US (ultrasound) education. The outcomes were compared between residency programs with and without EUS (emergency ultrasound) fellowships.
results.reference: Most clinicians did not change their CT scan ordering after receiving education about radiation from a radiologist. Radiation education allowed clinicians to discuss CT benefits and risks with their patients and to choose appropriate CT protocols. Referring physician groups are interested in this topic, and radiologists should be encouraged to give radiation lectures to them.

results.question: Does context matter for the relationship between deprivation and all-cause mortality?
rewritten_queries: deprivation all-cause mortality contextual factors
socioeconomic status mortality relationship context
area-level deprivation health outcomes mortality
results.answer:
The studies indicate that socio-economic deprivation is significantly correlated with all-cause mortality across different regions and ethnic groups. However, the relationship between deprivation and mortality does not vary spatially within Scotland, suggesting that the contextual geographic differences do not alter this relationship. Conversely, ethnic groups in New Zealand show different gradients of deprivation-related mortality, implying that context in terms of ethnicity and deprivation distribution does influence mortality outcomes.

no
contexts: A growing body of research emphasizes the importance of contextual factors on health outcomes. Using postcode sector data for Scotland (UK), this study tests the hypothesis of spatial heterogeneity in the relationship between area-level deprivation and mortality to determine if contextual differences in the West vs. the rest of Scotland influence this relationship. Research into health inequalities frequently fails to recognise spatial heterogeneity in the deprivation-health relationship, assuming that global relationships apply uniformly across geographical areas. In this study, exploratory spatial data analysis methods are used to assess local patterns in deprivation and mortality. Spatial regression models are then implemented to examine the relationship between deprivation and mortality more formally.

The initial exploratory spatial data analysis reveals concentrations of high standardized mortality ratios (SMR (standardized mortality ratios)) and deprivation (hotspots) in the West of Scotland and concentrations of low values (coldspots) for both variables in the rest of the country. The main spatial regression result is that deprivation is the only variable that is highly significantly correlated with all-cause mortality in all models. However, in contrast to the expected spatial heterogeneity in the deprivation-mortality relationship, this relation does not vary between regions in any of the models. This result is robust to a number of specifications, including weighting for population size, controlling for spatial autocorrelation and heteroskedasticity, assuming a non-linear relationship between mortality and socio-economic deprivation, separating the dependent variable into male and female SMRs, and distinguishing between West, North and Southeast regions. The rejection of the hypothesis of spatial heterogeneity in the relationship between socio-economic deprivation and mortality complements prior research on the stability of the deprivation-mortality relationship over time.

First, to establish whether a deprivation gradient in all-cause mortality exists for all ethnic groups within New Zealand; second, if such gradients do exist, whether their absolute slopes are the same; and third, if such gradients exist, what impact the unequal deprivation distributions of the different ethnic groups have on the observed ethnic inequalities in life expectancy at birth.

All four ethnic groups exhibit deprivation gradients in all-cause mortality (life expectancy). Maori show the steepest gradients, with slopes approximately 25% steeper than those of Europeans for both males and females. By contrast, gradients among Asian and Pacific peoples are shallower than those of their European counterparts.

Longitudinal data with 1990 census records being linked to mortality data up to 2005 were used (Swiss National Cohort). The sample comprised all residents over age 44 years in Switzerland (n=2,440,242). All-cause mortality HRs for marital status and living arrangements were estimated by Cox regression for men and women and different age groups with adjustment for education and socio-professional category.
results.reference: The homogeneity we found in the deprivation-mortality relationship across the regions of Scotland and the absence of a contextualized effect of region highlights the importance of taking a broader strategic policy that can combat the toxic impacts of socio-economic deprivation on health. Focusing on a few specific places (e.g. 15% of the poorest areas) to concentrate resources might be a good start but the impact of socio-economic deprivation on mortality is not restricted to a few places. A comprehensive strategy that can be sustained over time might be needed to interrupt the linkages between poverty and mortality.

results.question: Does stress increase imitation of drinking behavior?
rewritten_queries: stress influence drinking behavior
stress and alcohol consumption initiation
psychological stress alcohol use onset
results.answer:
The study described in abstracts [1], [2], and [3] directly tested whether stress influences the tendency to imitate others' drinking behavior. The results showed that participants drank more when confederates drank alcohol regardless of stress condition, and no difference was found between stress and no-stress groups. Therefore, stress did not moderate or increase imitation of drinking behavior.

no
contexts: That alcohol consumption is strongly influenced by the drinking behavior of social company has been demonstrated in observational research. However, not everyone is equally vulnerable to other people's drinking, and it is important to unravel which factors underlie these individual differences. This study focuses on the role of psychosocial stress in attempting to explain individual differences in the propensity to imitate alcohol consumption.

With a 2 (confederate's drinking condition: alcohol vs. soda) × 2 (participant's stress condition: stress vs. no stress) experimental design, we tested whether the tendency to imitate other people's drinking was related to participants' induced stress levels. The young male adults (N = 106) were randomly assigned to each of the conditions. In each session, directly after the stress or no-stress period, confederates and participants entered a bar laboratory where we observed their drinking behavior. Prior to entering the session, confederates were instructed to drink alcohol or soda.

Participants in both stress and no-stress conditions consumed substantially more alcohol when confederates drank alcohol than when they drank soda. There was no difference in alcohol consumed between stress and no-stress conditions. No moderating effect of stress on the tendency to drink along with peers was found.

Rats given 5 min of alcohol-associated cues responded significantly more on the active lever (26% increase) and consumed more alcohol as verified by increased blood alcohol levels (8.9 mM versus control 7.5 mM). Ten or 15 min of cues did not change alcohol consumption and 5 min in a novel environment decreased response by 66%. After a 10-day break in training, 5 min of alcohol-associated cues still increased alcohol consumption (29% increase) and the cue effect could be dose-dependently blocked by naltrexone (143% decrease at 0.03 mg/kg).

The interaction of family factors and pubertal stage did not improve the fit of the model, so a main effect model of family factors and pubertal stage was adopted. There were significant main effects for pubertal stage with boys in middle puberty at increased odds of alcohol use, and girls in advanced puberty at increased odds of alcohol use.
results.reference: Generally, it appears that among young male adults, imitation of alcohol consumption is a robust phenomenon not dependent on individual stress levels.

results.question: School food policy at Dutch primary schools: room for improvement?
rewritten_queries: Dutch primary school food policy
school nutrition guidelines Netherlands primary education
evaluation school food programs Dutch primary schools
results.answer:
The study shows that while most Dutch primary schools have a written food policy and principals believe sufficient attention is paid to nutrition, the rules are often not clearly defined. Additionally, there is variation in parental opinions on enforcement, and nearly half of the parents believe schools share responsibility for fostering healthy eating habits, indicating potential gaps in policy clarity and implementation.

yes
contexts: Schools can play an important role in the prevention of obesity, e.g. by providing an environment that stimulates healthy eating habits and by developing a food policy to provide such an environment. The effectiveness of a school food policy is affected by the content of the policy, its implementation and its support by parents, teachers and principals. The aim of this study is to detect opportunities to improve the school food policy and/or implementation at Dutch primary schools. Therefore, this study explores the school food policy and investigates schools' (teachers and principals) and parents' opinion on the school food policy.

Data on the schools' perspective of the food policy was collected from principals and teachers by means of semi-structured interviews. In total 74 principals and 72 teachers from 83 Dutch primary schools were interviewed. Data on parental perceptions about the school food policy were based on a cross-sectional survey among 1,429 parents from the same schools.

Most principals (87.1%) reported that their school had a written food policy; however in most cases the rules were not clearly defined. Most of the principals (87.8%) believed that their school paid sufficient attention to nutrition and health. Teachers and principals felt that parents were primarily responsible to encourage healthy eating habits among children, while 49.8% of the parents believed that it is also a responsibility of the school to foster healthy eating habits among children. Most parents reported that they appreciated the school food policy and comply with the food rules. Parents' opinion on the enforcement of the school food policy varied: 28.1% believed that the school should enforce the policy more strongly, 32.1% was satisfied, and 39.8% had no opinion on this topic.
Four primary care practices affiliated with the University of Nijmegen in the Netherlands.

Older patients from a Dutch outpatient clinic were invited to participate in a self-management intervention, and their characteristics were assessed. Demographic data were collected, as well as data on physical functioning and lack of emotional support. People who refused to participate were asked to give their reasons for refusing.
results.reference: Dutch primary schools could play a more important role in fostering healthy eating habits among children. The school food policy could be improved by clearly formulating food rules, simplifying supervision of the food rules, and defining how to enforce the food rules. In addition, the school food policy will only influence children's dietary behaviour if both the school and the parents support the policy.

results.question: Is the atopy patch test with house dust mites specific for atopic dermatitis?

diagnostic accuracy atopy patch test for atopic dermatitis
house dust mite allergen atopy patch test sensitivity specificity
results.answer:
The atopy patch test (APT) with house dust mites shows a significantly higher positivity rate and intensity in atopic dermatitis (AD) patients compared to non-AD subjects, indicating some level of specificity. However, positive responses were also observed in atopic subjects without eczema and in nonatopic individuals, suggesting that the test is not exclusively specific to AD.

no
contexts: The aim of this study was to evaluate the response to the APT (atopy patch test) with house dust mites (HDM (house dust mites)) in subjects nonaffected by AD (atopic dermatitis) and to compare the outcomes observed in these cases with those pointed out in AD (atopic dermatitis) patients, evaluating also the differences between two allergen extracts manufactured at different purifications and concentrations.

Forty-seven atopic subjects without eczema (AWE (atopic subjects without eczema)), 33 nonatopic (NA (nonatopic)) subjects and 77 adult AD (atopic dermatitis) patients were patch tested with an extract of purified bodies of HDM (house dust mites) at 20% and with another extract of whole bodies of HDM (house dust mites) at 30%, the latter corresponding to 300 microg/g of Der p 1. The reproducibility of APT (atopy patch test) was also tested in 8 AD (atopic dermatitis) patients, in 37 AWE (atopic subjects without eczema) subjects and in 19 NA (nonatopic) subjects.

The atopy patch test (APT (atopy patch test)), namely the patch test with aeroallergens, is regarded as specific for patients with atopic dermatitis (AD (atopic dermatitis)), but small numbers of positive APT (atopy patch test) were reported in the past also in atopic subjects without dermatitis and in healthy persons.

Positive responses with extract at 20% were observed in 29 (37.7%) AD (atopic dermatitis), in 5 (10.6%) AWE (atopic subjects without eczema) and in 4 (12.1%) NA (nonatopic) subjects. The APT (atopy patch test) with HDM (house dust mites) at 30% was positive in 32 (41.6%) AD (atopic dermatitis), 9 (19.1%) AWE (atopic subjects without eczema) and 4 (12.1%) NA (nonatopic) persons. The rates of positivity and the intensity scores of responses were significantly different between AD (atopic dermatitis) and non-AD (atopic dermatitis) subjects (p<0.01). The reproducibility of the APT (atopy patch test) in the three groups was satisfactory.

A median of two core samples per lesion provided for all the lesions a sensitivity for malignancy of 96.9%, specificity of 100%, false-positive rate of 0% and false-negative rate of 3.1%, and for the excised lesions a sensitivity of 96.5%, specificity of 100%, false-positive rate of 0%, false-negative rate of 3.5% and an underestimation rate of 3.4%.
results.reference: These observations lead to conclude that the APT with HDM is positive also in non-AD subjects but it is probably more specific for AD.

results.question: Juvenile osteochondritis dissecans: is it a growth disturbance of the secondary physis of the epiphysis?
rewritten_queries: juvenile osteochondritis dissecans pathophysiology
juvenile osteochondritis dissecans growth disturbance secondary physis epiphysis
juvenile osteochondritis dissecans epiphyseal involvement
results.answer:
The provided abstracts indicate that juvenile osteochondritis dissecans (OCD) is associated with disruption of the secondary physis of the epiphysis, as shown by significant differences in secondary physeal disruption on MRI in affected children compared to controls. This supports the hypothesis that juvenile OCD results from a growth disturbance of the secondary physis.

yes
contexts: The primary physis is responsible for longitudinal bone growth. Similarly, epiphysial growth relies on endochondral ossification from the circumferential secondary physeal [corrected]. injury can result in disruption of normal ossification. The cause of juvenile osteochondritis dissecans (OCD (osteochondritis dissecans)) remains elusive. We hypothesized that juvenile OCD (osteochondritis dissecans) results from an insult affecting endochondral ossification from the secondary physis. The purpose of our study was to evaluate the MRI (magnetic resonance imaging) appearance of the distal femoral epiphysis-particularly the secondary physis-of children with juvenile OCD (osteochondritis dissecans) and to compare these findings with the MRI (magnetic resonance imaging) findings of unaffected children.

All children were skeletally immature. Condylar lesions were medial in 24 knees and lateral in six knees. All were in the middle one third, posterior one third, or middle and posterior thirds in the sagittal plane. The majority of lesions spanned the intercondylar and middle one third of the femoral condyle in the coronal plane (73%). There was a significant difference between secondary physeal [corrected] disruption in juvenile OCD (osteochondritis dissecans) condyles compared with unaffected condyles (p<0.001) and control condyles (p<0.001). Compared with unaffected and control condyles, the OCD (osteochondritis dissecans) group showed chondroepiphysial widening (p<0.001) and subchondral bone edema (p<0.001) on MRI (magnetic resonance imaging). Neither chondroepiphysial integrity nor chondroepiphysial contour was significantly different between groups (p = 0.21, p = 0.31, respectively).

Knee MRI (magnetic resonance imaging) examinations of 30 children (age range, 8 years 8 months to 13 years 4 months) with OCD (osteochondritis dissecans) and 30 matched control patients were evaluated for skeletal maturity; location of the OCD (osteochondritis dissecans) lesion, if present; secondary physeal [corrected] continuity; overlying chondroepiphysial integrity, contour, and width; signal intensity of subchondral bone; and secondary physeal [corrected]conspicuity. Variables were compared using chi-square tests.

The aetiology of osteochondritis dissecans is still unclear. The aim of this prospective pilot study was to analyse whether vitamin D insufficiency, or deficiency, might be a contributing etiological factor in the development of an OCD lesion.

The patients' mean age was 31.3 years and most of them already exhibited closed epiphyseal plates. In the majority of patients (18/23), a distinct vitamin D3 deficiency was found, two patients were vitamin D3-insufficient and, in three patients, the vitamin D3 level reached the lowest normal value.
results.reference: MRI of children with OCD consistently showed secondary physis disruption, overlying chondroepiphysial widening, and subchondral bone edema. We suggest that disruption of normal endochondral ossification may be associated with juvenile OCD.

results.question: Do preoperative statins reduce atrial fibrillation after coronary artery bypass grafting?
