results.answer:
The provided studies show that preoperative statin therapy is associated with a significantly lower incidence of postoperative atrial fibrillation after coronary artery bypass grafting (16% in the statin group vs. 33% in the non-statin group, p = 0.005). Multivariate analysis also identified preoperative statin therapy as an independent predictor for reduced AF development (OR 0.327, p = 0.05), supporting the efficacy of statins in reducing AF after CABG.

yes
contexts: Recent studies have demonstrated that statins have pleiotropic effects, including anti-inflammatory effects and atrial fibrillation (AF (atrial fibrillation)) preventive effects. The objective of this study was to assess the efficacy of preoperative statin therapy in preventing AF (atrial fibrillation) after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG (coronary artery bypass grafting)).

The overall incidence of postoperative AF (atrial fibrillation) was 26%. Postoperative AF (atrial fibrillation) was significantly lower in the Statin group compared with the Non-statin group (16% versus 33%, p = 0.005). Multivariate analysis demonstrated that independent predictors of AF (atrial fibrillation) development after CABG (coronary artery bypass grafting) were preoperative statin therapy (odds ratio [OR]0.327, 95% confidence interval [CI (confidence interval)] 0.107 to 0.998, p = 0.05) and age (OR 1.058, 95% CI (confidence interval) 1.004 to 1.116, p = 0.035).

221 patients underwent CABG (coronary artery bypass grafting) in our hospital from 2004 to 2007. 14 patients with preoperative AF (atrial fibrillation) and 4 patients with concomitant valve surgery were excluded from this study. Patients were divided into two groups to examine the influence of statins: those with preoperative statin therapy (Statin group, n = 77) and those without it (Non-statin group, n = 126). In addition, patients were divided into two groups to determine the independent predictors for postoperative AF (atrial fibrillation): those with postoperative AF (AF (atrial fibrillation) group, n = 54) and those without it (Non-AF (atrial fibrillation) group, n = 149). Patient data were collected and analyzed retrospectively.

Aortoplasty was associated with aortic valve replacement in 47 cases (35 mechanical vs 12 biological), subvalvular myectomy in 29 cases, and CABG (coronary artery bypass graft) in 13 cases. The procedure was performed with low hospital mortality (2%) and a low postoperative morbidity. Computertomographic and echocardiographic diameters were significantly smaller after reduction (55.8+/-9mm down to 40.51+/-6.2mm (CT), p<0.002; 54.1+/-6.7mm preoperatively down to 38.7+/-7.1mm (echocardiography), p<0.002), with stable performance in long-term follow-up (mean follow-up time: 70 months).

Atrial fibrillation, which occurs in 12% of all major foregut surgeries, can prolong hospital stay and increase morbidity. Minimally invasive techniques in foregut surgery have been suggested to cause less tissue trauma. We examined the factors associated with new-onset atrial fibrillation after foregut surgery at our institution.
results.reference: Our study indicated that preoperative statin therapy seems to reduce AF development after CABG.

results.question: Is there a uniform basal endometrial gene expression profile during the implantation window in women who became pregnant in a subsequent ICSI cycle?

The study analyzed 43 genes during the window of implantation in women who subsequently became pregnant after ICSI. contexts: To understand which genes are really involved in the implantation process, we planned to study the gene basal expression profile during the window of implantation (WOI (window of implantation)) of patients who became pregnant in a subsequent ICSI cycle.

Women attending their first ICSI cycle at ANDROS Day Surgery for severe male factor infertility were included in the study. Do endometrial polyps from pre- and post-menopausal women have similar immunohistochemical expression of oestrogen and progesterone receptors (ER (emergency room), PR) and markers of cellular proliferation/apoptosis (Ki67 and Bcl-2).

Endometrial polyps from pre- and post-menopausal women had significant differences in their expression of hormone receptors and Ki67. However, polyps from both groups of women had similarly increased levels of Bcl-2, an inhibitor of apoptosis.
results.reference: Our data suggest that very few genes, which change their expression level during the WOI, show a quantitative homogeneous expression in endometrially-receptive patients. In conclusion, in this study only six genes showed a homogeneous expression, and are probably involved in embryo implantation mechanisms.

results.question: Can decisional algorithms replace global introspection in the individual causality assessment of spontaneously reported ADRs?

results.answer:
The evidence shows that decisional algorithms have high sensitivity (93%) but very low specificity (7%) compared to the global introspection method, indicating they often classify reports as drug-related even when they are not. This suggests that algorithms cannot reliably replace global introspection for individual causality assessment due to poor specificity. contexts: Peripheral venous thrombophlebitis (PVT (peripheral venous thrombophlebitis)) is a common complication of intravenous cannulation, occurring in about 30% of patients. We evaluated the effect of elective re-siting of intravenous cannulae every 48 hours on the incidence and severity of PVT (peripheral venous thrombophlebitis) in patients receiving intravenous fluids/drugs.

We randomized 42 patients who were admitted for major abdominal surgery to either the control or study group (n = 21 in either group). Informed consent was obtained from all of them. Cannulae in the control group were removed only if the site became painful, the cannula got dislodged or there were signs and symptoms suggestive of PVT (peripheral venous thrombophlebitis), namely pain, erythema, swelling, excessive warmth or a palpable venous cord. Cannulae in the study group were changed and re-sited electively every 48 hours. All the patients were examined every 24 hours for signs and symptoms of PVT (peripheral venous thrombophlebitis) at the current and previous sites of infusion.

The incidence of PVT (peripheral venous thrombophlebitis) was 100% (21/21) in the control group and only 9.5% (2/21) in the study group (p<0.0001). The severity of PVT (peripheral venous thrombophlebitis) was also less in the study group compared with that in the control group. Day-wise correlation of the incidence of PVT (peripheral venous thrombophlebitis) showed that 82.6% of the episodes of PVT (peripheral venous thrombophlebitis) occurred on day 3.

This randomized single-blinded single-center clinical trial involved 320 patients undergoing elective PCI (percutaneous coronary intervention) who were randomized to either receive three 5-min cycles of ischemia by inflation of a cuff on the non-dominant arm to 200 mm Hg (remote postischemic conditioning) or to placebo (uninflated cuff). The primary outcome variable was the maximum increase in troponin in the first 24 h. The secondary outcome variable was readmission due to heart failure or cardiovascular mortality after 1 year of follow-up. In addition, a diabetic population was studied.

The morning following cardiac surgery, simultaneous arterial line and peripheral venous blood samples were taken for activated plasma thromboplastin time (APTT (activated plasma thromboplastin time)) ratio and international normalized ratio (INR (international normalized ratio)) in 49 randomly selected patients. Also, a thromboelastogram analysis (TEG (thromboelastogram analysis)) (n = 7) was made. A survey of 22 UK cardiothoracic intensive care units was carried out to determine the practice for the withdrawal of blood for clotting studies.
results.reference: Elective re-siting of intravenous cannulae every 48 hours results in a significant reduction in the incidence and severity of PVT. We recommend that this should be adopted as standard practice in managing all patients who require prolonged intravenous therapy.

results.reference: The menopausal transition warrants attention as a period of vulnerability to MDD recurrence, while health factors and VMS should be considered important risk factors for first lifetime-onset of MDD during midlife.

Ventricular arrhythmias were well tolerated in all patients except in cases of early perioperative right ventricular failure, with no deaths. results.question: Can dobutamine stress echocardiography induce cardiac troponin elevation?

In 57 patients undergoing DSE, none showed elevated cTnI 18-24 hours after the test, despite some having ischemia during the procedure. This evidence suggests that DSE does not induce cardiac troponin elevation.

Among the patients with established ischemia on DSE (dobutamine stress echo), 12 (22%) had mild ischemia, 13 (23.6%) had moderate and 5 (9%) had severe ischemia. Angiography was performed in 13 (26%) of the patients, of which 7 had PCI (percutaneous coronary intervention) and one was referred to bypass surgery. This randomized single-blinded single-center clinical trial involved 320 patients undergoing elective PCI (percutaneous coronary intervention) who were randomized to either receive three 5-min cycles of ischemia by inflation of a cuff on the non-dominant arm to 200 mm Hg (remote postischemic conditioning) or to placebo (uninflated cuff). The primary outcome variable was the maximum increase in troponin in the first 24 h. The secondary outcome variable was readmission due to heart failure or cardiovascular mortality after 1 year of follow-up. In addition, a diabetic population was studied.
results.reference: Our results indicate that there is no elevation of cTn despite the occurrence of significant WMAs on DSE. We conclude that cTnI cannot be used as an additional diagnostic tool during pharmacological stress test performed to evaluate the presence and severity of ischemia.

results.reference: Although initial infection control rate was substantially lower in the retention group than the removal group, final results were comparable at latest followup. Specifically, obese individuals at 11 years had a 50% greater prevalence of wheezing at 15 years and a higher risk of persistent wheezing, supporting obesity as a risk factor for wheezing in adolescents.

yes
contexts: To investigate the effect of obesity at the start of adolescence on the prevalence, incidence and maintenance of chest wheezing among individuals aged 11-15 years in a birth cohort in a developing country.

The seventh follow-up of the 1993 Pelotas birth cohort occurred in 2004 (individuals aged 10-11 years). Between January and August 2008, the eighth follow-up of the cohort was conducted. All the individuals of the original cohort who were alive (who were then adolescents aged between 14 and 15 years) were targets for the study. The International Study of Asthma and Allergies in Childhood (ISAAC (international study of asthma and allergies in childhood)) questionnaire was used to define wheezing. In addition to the body mass index (BMI (body mass index)), used to define obesity by the World Health Organization (WHO (world health organization)) criteria, we assessed skinfold thickness.

From the original cohort, 4,349 individuals were located (85.7% follow-up rate). The prevalence of chest wheezing at 11 and 15 years were 13.5% (95% CI (confidence interval): 12.5%-14.5%) and 12.1% (95% CI (confidence interval): 11.1%-13.1%), respectively. The prevalence of wheezing at both times was 4.5% (95% CI (confidence interval): 3.9%-5.1%) and the incidence of wheezing was 7.5% (95% CI (confidence interval): 6.7%-8.3%). Independent of the effect of various confounding variables, the prevalence of wheezing at 15 years was 50% greater among obese individuals than among eutrophic individuals at 11 years (RR (relative risk) 1.53; 95% CI (confidence interval): 1.14-2.05). The greater the skinfold tertile at 11 years, the higher the prevalence of wheezing at 15 years was (p = .011). Weight status and skinfolds did not present any association with incident wheezing. After controlling for confounding factors, the risk of persistent wheezing among obese individuals at 11 years was 1.82 (95% CI (confidence interval): 1.30-2.54).

It has been suggested that increasing obesity levels in young women lead to intrauterine environments that, in turn, stimulate increased obesity among their offspring, generating an intergenerational acceleration of obesity levels. If this mechanism is important, the association of maternal body mass index (BMI (body mass index)) with offspring BMI (body mass index) should be stronger than the association of paternal with offspring BMI (body mass index).

To provide insight into the factors by which obesity in itself may directly lead to early arterial damage, we aimed to determine early sonographic markers of obesity-related vascular dysfunction in young obese males.
results.reference: Since obesity at the start of adolescence is associated with asthma symptom persistence, prevention and treatment of obesity may reduce avoidable healthcare costs and disease burden.

Using EtCO2 ranges of 30 to 50 mmHg, the capnographic method was able to identify 84% of instances where PaCO(2) was between 35 (<35 = hypocarbia) and 55 mmHg (>55= hypercapnia).

Secondhand smoke exposure (SHSe (secondhand smoke exposure)) threatens fragile infants discharged from a neonatal intensive care unit (NICU (neonatal intensive care unit)). To compare two treatment strategies in preterm infants with or at risk of respiratory distress syndrome: early surfactant administration (within one hour of birth) versus late surfactant administration, in a geographically defined population.
results.reference: There is good correlation and agreement between end-tidal CO(2) and arterial CO(2) in ELBW infants in the EtCO(2) range 30-50 mmHg. End-tidal CO(2) monitoring can be helpful in trending or for screening abnormal PaCO(2) values in ELBW infants in first week of life.

High CA125 concentrations were observed in patients with ovarian endometriosis and in those with ovarian cancer. A marked difference in CA72-4 values was observed between women with ovarian cancer (71.0%) and patients with endometriosis (13.8%) (P<0.0001).

results.question: Preservation of the PCL when performing cruciate-retaining TKA: Is the tibial tuberosity a reliable predictor of the PCL footprint location?

tibial tuberosity predictor PCL footprint location

results.answer:
The studies indicate that the tibial tuberosity can be used as a referencing landmark to estimate the PCL footprint height prior to tibial cut, with measured distances between the tibial tuberosity and PCL footprint provided. However, there is a noted risk of partial or total PCL removal depending on the vertical distance, suggesting that while the tibial tuberosity is somewhat predictive, it may not be perfectly reliable in all cases. Overall, the evidence supports the tibial tuberosity as a useful predictor for the PCL footprint location.

yes
contexts: Reconstruction of the joint line is crucial in total knee arthroplasty (TKA (total knee arthroplasty)). A routine height of tibial cut to maintain the natural joint line may compromise the preservation of the PCL. Since the PCL footprint is not accessible prior to tibial osteotomy, it seems beneficial to identify a reliable extraarticular anatomic landmark for predicting the PCL footprint and being visible within standard TKA (total knee arthroplasty) approach. The fibula head predicts reliably the location of PCL footprint; however, it is not accessible during TKA (total knee arthroplasty). The aim of this study now was to analyze whether the tibial tuberosity can serve as a reliable referencing landmark to estimate the PCL footprint height prior to tibial cut.

The vertical distance between the tibial tuberosity and tibial cut averaged 24.7 ± 4 mm. The average vertical distance from tibial tuberosity to proximal and to distal PCL footprint was found to be 22 ± 4.4 and 16 ± 4.4 mm, respectively. Five knees were considered at 50% risk of an entire PCL removal after CR TKA (total knee arthroplasty).

The first consecutive case series included 216 CR TKA (total knee arthroplasty). Standing postoperative lateral view radiographs were utilized to measure the vertical distance between tibial tuberosity and tibial osteotomy plane. In the second case series, 223 knee MRIs were consecutively analyzed to measure the vertical distance between tibial tuberosity and PCL footprint. The probability of partial or total PCL removal was calculated for different vertical distances between tibial tuberosity and tibial cutting surface.

We reviewed the records of 60 patients treated for 64 infected TKA from 2002 to 2007. Twenty-eight patients (32 knees) underwent débridement with retention of component, and 32 patients (32 knees) were treated with component removal and two-stage revision surgery. We determined patients' demographics, type of infection, causative organisms, and outcome of treatment. Mean followup was 36 months (range, 12-84 months).

Six human cadaver knees were tested before implantation, after implantation with a bicruciate-retaining unicompartmental knee prosthesis, and after implantation with a posterior cruciate-retaining tricompartmental knee prosthesis. The unicompartmental prosthesis was initially implanted, and it was then revised to a total condylar knee replacement. The knee kinematics were measured with use of an electromagnetic tracking device while the knee was put through dynamic simulated stair-climbing under peak flexion moments of approximately 40 N-m. Quadriceps tension was also measured for all three conditions.
results.reference: Current surgical techniques of tibial preparation may result in partial or total PCL damage. Tibial tuberosity is a useful anatomical landmark to locate the PCL footprint and to predict the probability of its detachment pre-, intra-, and postoperatively. This knowledge might be useful to predict and avoid instability, consecutive pain, and dissatisfaction after TKA related to PCL insufficiency.

results.question: The English antibiotic awareness campaigns: did they change the public's knowledge of and attitudes to antibiotic use?

results.answer:
The 2008 English antibiotic awareness campaigns led to a small increase in recollection of campaign posters and more frequent advice to use other remedies for coughs and colds, but there was no detected improvement in understanding the lack of benefit of antibiotics for coughs and colds or in antibiotic use. Therefore, the campaigns did not significantly change the public's knowledge or attitudes toward antibiotic use.

no
contexts: English and Scottish (acting as controls) adults aged>or = 15 years were questioned face to face about their attitudes to and use of antibiotics, in January 2008 (1888) before and in January 2009 (1830) after the antibiotic campaigns.
To determine the effect of the 2008 English public antibiotic campaigns.

Among English respondents, there was a small increase in recollection of campaign posters (2009 23.7% versus 2008 19.2%; P = 0.03), but this increase was only 2.3% higher in England than in Scotland. We did not detect any improvement in either England or Scotland, or any differences between England and Scotland in the understanding of the lack of benefit of antibiotics for coughs and colds, and we found no improvement in antibiotic use. We detected a significant increase in respondents retaining leftover antibiotics. Over 20% reported discussing antibiotics with their general practitioner (GP (general practitioner)) or nurse in the year to January 2009. The offer of a delayed antibiotic prescription was reported significantly more often by English respondents (19% versus 8% Scottish in 2009; P = 0.01), and English respondents were advised to use other remedies for coughs and colds significantly more often in the year to January 2009 (12.7% in 2009 versus 7.4% in 2008; P<0.001).

Little is known about the validity and reliability of expert assessments of the quality of antimicrobial prescribing, despite their importance in antimicrobial stewardship. We investigated how infectious disease doctors' assessments compared with a reference standard (modal expert opinion) and with the assessments of their colleagues.
Surveyed Medicare beneficiaries in 5 areas; clustered unvaccinated seniors by their immunization related knowledge and attitudes.
results.reference: There is little evidence that the 2008 public antibiotic campaigns were effective. The use and visibility of future campaign materials needs auditing. A carefully planned approach that targets the public in GP waiting rooms and through clinicians in consultations may be a more effective way of improving prudent antibiotic use.

Pain relief was complete in 57 patients (45 without medication and 12 with low-dose medication), partial in 15, and minimal in another 15 patients. results.question: Should tumor depth be included in prognostication of soft tissue sarcoma?

results.answer:
The provided studies indicate that tumor depth does not have a major independent prognostic effect when tumor grade and size are accounted for. The poorer prognosis associated with deep tumors appears to be due to their larger size rather than depth itself, suggesting that depth alone should not be included in prognostication.

no
contexts: Most staging systems for soft tissue sarcoma are based on histologic malignancy-grade, tumor size and tumor depth. These factors are generally dichotomized, size at 5 cm. We believe it is unlikely that tumor depth per se should influence a tumor's metastatic capability. Therefore we hypothesized that the unfavourable prognostic importance of depth could be explained by the close association between size and depth, deep-seated tumors on average being larger than the superficial ones. When tumor size is dichotomized, this effect should be most pronounced in the large size (>5 cm) group in which the size span is larger.

We analyzed the associations between tumor size and depth and the prognostic importance of grade, size and depth in a population-based series of 490 adult patients with soft tissue sarcoma of the extremity or trunk wall with complete, 4.5 years minimum, follow-up.

Multivariate analysis showed no major prognostic effect of tumor depth when grade and size were taken into account. The mean size of small tumors was the same whether superficial or deep but the mean size of large and deep-seated tumors were one third larger than that of large but superficial tumors. Tumor depth influenced the prognosis in the subset of high-grade and large tumors. In this subset deep-seated tumors had poorer survival rate than superficial tumors, which could be explained by the larger mean size of the deep-seated tumors.

A total of 680 eligible cases were classified into three groups (surveillance, opportunistic, and symptomatic groups) according to their initial exposure. We used survival time, tumor morphology, and T staging as prognostic outcomes. This metastasis rate was significantly correlated with pT stage, the lobe where the tumor was located, metastasis status of intrapulmonary lymph nodes, pTNM stage, and most of the other mediastinal lymph node stations. results.reference: Most of the prognostic value of tumor depth in soft tissue sarcomas of the extremity or trunk wall can be explained by the association between tumor size and depth.

results.question: Is amoxapine an atypical antipsychotic?

To estimate healthcare costs and utilization of AAPs (atypical antipsychotics) compared to other second-line agents.

results.reference: PET data show that amoxapine's profile is very similar to that of the established atypical antipsychotics. results.question: Is non-HDL-cholesterol a better predictor of long-term outcome in patients after acute myocardial infarction compared to LDL-cholesterol?

results.answer:
The study found that patients with non-HDL-C >130 mg/dl had a significantly higher incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), while surprisingly, LDL-C >100 mg/dl was associated with a reduced risk of MACE compared to LDL-C <70 mg/dl. This suggests that non-HDL-C is a better predictor of long-term outcomes after acute myocardial infarction than LDL-C in this patient population.

yes
contexts: It has recently been shown that non-high density lipoprotein cholesterol (non-HDL (high density lipoprotein)-C) may be a better predictor of cardiovascular risk than low density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL (low density lipoprotein)-C). Based on known ethic differences in lipid parameters and cardiovascular risk prediction, we sought to study the predictability of attaining non-HDL (high density lipoprotein)-C target and long-term major adverse cardiovascular event (MACE (major adverse cardiovascular event)) in Thai patients after acute myocardial infarction (AMI (acute myocardial infarction)) compared to attaining LDL (low density lipoprotein)-C target.

We retrospectively obtained the data of all patients who were admitted at Maharaj Nakorn Chiang Mai hospital due to AMI (acute myocardial infarction) during 2006-2013. The mean non-HDL (high density lipoprotein)-C and LDL (low density lipoprotein)-C during long-term follow-up were used to predict MACE (major adverse cardiovascular event) at each time point. The patients were classified as target attainment if non-HDL (high density lipoprotein)-C <100 mg/dl and/or LDL (low density lipoprotein)-C <70 mg/dl. The MACE (major adverse cardiovascular event) was defined as combination of all-cause death, nonfatal coronary event and nonfatal stroke.

During mean follow-up of 2.6 ± 1.6 years among 868 patients after AMI (acute myocardial infarction), 34.4% achieved non-HDL (high density lipoprotein)-C target, 23.7% achieved LDL (low density lipoprotein)-C target and 21.2% experienced MACEs. LDL (low density lipoprotein)-C and non-HDL (high density lipoprotein)-C were directly compared in Cox regression model. Compared with non-HDL (high density lipoprotein)-C <100 mg/dl, patients with non-HDL (high density lipoprotein)-C of>130 mg/dl had higher incidence of MACEs (HR 3.15, 95% CI (confidence interval) 1.46-6.80, P = 0.003). Surprisingly, LDL (low density lipoprotein)-C >100 mg/dl was associated with reduced risk of MACE (major adverse cardiovascular event) as compared to LDL (low density lipoprotein) <70 mg/dl (HR 0.42, 95% CI (confidence interval) 0.18-0.98, p = 0.046) after direct pairwise comparison with non-HDL (high density lipoprotein)-C level.

Weekend AMI (acute myocardial infarction) patients are significantly less likely to receive immediate intensive cardiac procedures, and experience significantly higher rates of adverse health outcomes. Weekend admission leads to a 3.47 percentage point reduction in catheterization at 1 day, a 1.52 point reduction in angioplasty, and a 0.35 point reduction in by-pass surgery (p<.001 in all cases). The primary effect is delayed treatment, as weekend-weekday procedure differentials narrow over time from the initial hospitalization. Weekend patients experience a 0.38 percentage point (p<.001) increase in 1-year mortality and a 0.20 point (p<.001) increase in 1-year readmission with congestive heart failure.

The role of early revascularization among patients with acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock remains controversial. Angioplasty registries, while suggesting a benefit, are subject to selection bias, and clinical trials have been underpowered to detect early benefits. The provided studies indicate that there are no significant differences in neuropsychological test performance between patients who experienced loss of consciousness (LOC) and those who did not after head injury. results.reference: The results of this study cast doubt on the importance of LOC as a predictor of neuropsychological test performance during the acute phase of recovery from mild traumatic brain injury. Neuropsychological testing procedures have been shown to be sensitive in measuring cognitive sequelae of mild traumatic brain injury (concussion) in athletes. The failure of this study to find any relationship between LOC and neuropsychological functioning in a large sample of patients with mild head trauma calls into question the assignment of primary importance to LOC in grading severity of concussion.
